148	// ============================================================
149	// Policy definition
150	// ============================================================
151	//
152	// Principle of least privilege:
153	//  - Every permission is explicitly listed (no wildcard / "all" grants).
154	//  - Permissions are additive; roles cannot negate another role's grants.
155	//  - RolesWrite is withheld from all predefined roles — it must be granted
156	//    only via a separate super-admin provisioning path (out of scope here).
157	//
158	// Role summary:
159	//   Operations Admin  — full ops domain, limited payment read, audit & user management
160	//   Dispatcher        — ops read/write (no delete/publish), own notifications
161	//   Finance Analyst   — full payments domain, ops read for reference
162	//   Staff User        — read-only ops, own inbox, basic reporting
163	
164	fn build_map() -> HashMap<&'static str, PermSet> {
165	    use Permission::*;
166	
167	    let mut m: HashMap<&'static str, PermSet> = HashMap::new();
168	
169	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
170	    // Operations Admin  (27 permissions)
171	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
172	    m.insert(ROLE_OPERATIONS_ADMIN, HashSet::from([
173	        // Full ops control
174	        OpsRoutesRead, OpsRoutesWrite, OpsRoutesDelete,
175	        OpsStopsRead,  OpsStopsWrite,  OpsStopsDelete,
176	        OpsTripsRead,  OpsTripsWrite,  OpsTripsDelete,
177	        OpsConfigRead, OpsConfigWrite, OpsConfigPublish,
178	        // Full notification management + announcement broadcast
179	        NotificationsInboxRead, NotificationsReadAll,
180	        NotificationsSubscriptionsManage, NotificationsDndManage,
181	        SysAnnouncementWrite,
182	        // Payment visibility + refund approval (no financial write authority)
183	        PaymentsTransactionsRead,
184	        PaymentsRefundsRead, PaymentsRefundsApprove,
185	        PaymentsReconciliationRead,
186	        // Reporting (including metric definition management)
187	        ReportingRead, ReportingExport, ReportingMetricsManage,
188	        // Audit trail visibility
189	        AuditRead,
190	        // User management (not RolesWrite — role schema changes require deployment)
191	        UsersRead, UsersWrite, UsersDelete, RolesRead,
192	    ]));
193	
194	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
195	    // Dispatcher  (11 permissions)
196	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
197	    m.insert(ROLE_DISPATCHER, HashSet::from([
198	        // Ops read/write — no delete, no config publish
199	        OpsRoutesRead, OpsRoutesWrite,
200	        OpsStopsRead,  OpsStopsWrite,
201	        OpsTripsRead,  OpsTripsWrite,
202	        OpsConfigRead,
203	        // Own notifications
204	        NotificationsInboxRead,
205	        NotificationsSubscriptionsManage,
206	        NotificationsDndManage,
207	        // Operational reports (read-only)
208	        ReportingRead,
209	    ]));
210	
211	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
212	    // Finance Analyst  (16 permissions)
213	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
214	    m.insert(ROLE_FINANCE_ANALYST, HashSet::from([
215	        // Ops read — reference data needed for trip-to-payment correlation
216	        OpsRoutesRead, OpsTripsRead,
217	        // Own notifications
218	        NotificationsInboxRead,
219	        NotificationsSubscriptionsManage,
220	        NotificationsDndManage,
221	        // Full payments domain
222	        PaymentsTransactionsRead, PaymentsTransactionsWrite,
223	        PaymentsRefundsRead,      PaymentsRefundsWrite, PaymentsRefundsApprove,
224	        PaymentsReconciliationRead, PaymentsReconciliationRun,
225	        PaymentsStatementsRead,   PaymentsStatementsImport,
226	        // Reporting with export (for external reconciliation review)
227	        ReportingRead, ReportingExport, ReportingMetricsManage,
228	    ]));
229	
230	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
231	    // Staff User  (5 permissions)
232	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
233	    m.insert(ROLE_STAFF_USER, HashSet::from([
234	        // Read-only operational access
235	        OpsRoutesRead, OpsTripsRead,
236	        // Own inbox + DND only (no subscription management)
237	        NotificationsInboxRead, NotificationsDndManage,
238	        // Basic reporting
239	        ReportingRead,
240	    ]));
241	
242	    m
243	}

157	/// POST /payments/callbacks/{gateway}
158	///
159	/// Receives an inbound webhook from a payment provider.
160	/// Pipeline:
161	///   1. Extract signature, nonce, timestamp from headers (per gateway config).
162	///   2. Verify signature + anti-replay (timestamp window + nonce uniqueness).
163	///   3. Insert callback record.
164	///   4. Attempt to match against a pending transaction and update its status.
165	pub async fn receive_callback(
166	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
167	    req:     HttpRequest,
168	    path:    web::Path<String>,
169	    body:    web::Bytes,
170	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
171	    let gateway_name = path.into_inner();
172	    let gw = load_gateway(&state.db, &gateway_name).await
173	        .map_err(AppError::from)?;
174	
175	    // ---- Extract anti-replay headers ----
176	    let get_header = |name: &str| -> Result<String, AppError> {
177	        req.headers()
178	            .get(name)
179	            .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
180	            .map(str::to_string)
181	            .ok_or_else(|| AppError::BadRequest(
182	                format!("Missing required header: {}", name)
183	            ))
184	    };
185	
186	    let signature  = get_header(gw.sig_header())?;
187	    let nonce      = get_header(gw.nonce_header())?;
188	    let ts_str     = get_header(gw.ts_header())?;
189	    let timestamp: i64 = ts_str.parse().map_err(|_|
190	        AppError::BadRequest("Invalid timestamp header (expected integer seconds)".to_string())
191	    )?;
192	
193	    // ---- Verify signature + anti-replay ----
194	    verify_callback(&state.db, &gw, &body, &nonce, timestamp, &signature)
195	        .await
196	        .map_err(AppError::from)?;
197	
198	    // ---- Parse payload (best-effort; store raw bytes even if unparseable) ----
199	    let payload: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&body).unwrap_or(
200	        serde_json::json!({ "_raw": hex::encode(&body) })
201	    );
202	    let payload_hash = sig_sha256_hex(&body);
203	    let callback_ts: DateTime<Utc> = chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp(timestamp, 0)
204	        .unwrap_or_else(Utc::now);
205	
206	    // ---- Match against an existing transaction ----
207	    let txn_ref      = payload.get("transaction_ref")
208	        .or_else(|| payload.get("out_trade_no"))
209	        .or_else(|| payload.get("transaction_id"))
210	        .and_then(|v| v.as_str());
211	
212	    let transaction_id: Option<Uuid> = if let Some(ref_val) = txn_ref {
213	        sqlx::query_scalar!(
214	            "SELECT id FROM payments.transactions WHERE idempotency_key = $1 LIMIT 1",
215	            ref_val,
216	        )
217	        .fetch_optional(&state.db)
218	        .await
219	        .ok()
220	        .flatten()
221	    } else {
222	        None
223	    };
224	
225	    // ---- Insert callback record ----
226	    let callback_id = sqlx::query_scalar!(
227	        r#"
228	        INSERT INTO payments.callbacks
229	            (transaction_id, nonce, signature, payload_hash,
230	             payload, source, callback_timestamp, status)
231	        VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, 'received')
232	        RETURNING id
233	        "#,
234	        transaction_id,
235	        nonce,
236	        signature,
237	        payload_hash,
238	        payload,
239	        gateway_name,
240	        callback_ts,
241	    )
242	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
243	    .await?;
244	
245	    // ---- Promote transaction status based on callback ----
246	    if let Some(tx_id) = transaction_id {
247	        let cb_status = payload.get("status")
248	            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
249	            .unwrap_or("");
250	
251	        let new_tx_status = if cb_status.to_uppercase().starts_with("FAIL") {
252	            "failed"
253	        } else if cb_status.to_uppercase().starts_with("SUCCESS")
254	               || cb_status.to_uppercase() == "PAID"
255	               || cb_status.to_uppercase() == "COMPLETED" {
256	            "completed"
257	        } else {
258	            // Unknown status — leave transaction unchanged
259	            ""
260	        };
261	
262	        if !new_tx_status.is_empty() {
263	            sqlx::query!(
264	                r#"UPDATE payments.transactions
265	                   SET status = $2, updated_at = now()
266	                   WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'pending'"#,
267	                tx_id,
268	                new_tx_status,
269	            )
270	            .execute(&state.db)
271	            .await?;
272	        }
273	
274	        // Mark callback processed
275	        sqlx::query!(
276	            r#"UPDATE payments.callbacks
277	               SET status = 'processed', processed_at = now()
278	               WHERE id = $1"#,
279	            callback_id,
280	        )
281	        .execute(&state.db)
282	        .await?;
283	    }
284	
285	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(serde_json::json!({
286	        "callback_id": callback_id,
287	        "status":      "received",
288	    })))
289	}

358	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(serde_json::json!({

360	        "transaction_id": body.transaction_id,
361	        "status":         "processed",

583	pub async fn create_refund(
584	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,

625	        RefundRow,
626	        r#"
627	        INSERT INTO payments.refunds

752	/// In production this would call the payment provider's refund API; here it
753	/// is a synchronous state machine for offline operation.
754	pub async fn process_refund(
755	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
756	    session: AuthSession,
757	    path:    web::Path<Uuid>,
758	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
759	    session.require(Permission::PaymentsRefundsApprove)?;
760	    let id = *path;
761	
762	    let existing = sqlx::query!(
763	        "SELECT status, transaction_id, amount FROM payments.refunds WHERE id = $1",
764	        id,
765	    )
766	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
767	    .await?
768	    .ok_or_else(|| AppError::BadRequest("Refund not found".to_string()))?;
769	
770	    if existing.status != "approved" {
771	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!(
772	            "Refund cannot be processed from status '{}' (must be approved)", existing.status
773	        )));
774	    }
775	
776	    // Process: mark 'completed' and update the parent transaction
777	    let row = sqlx::query_as!(
778	        RefundRow,
779	        r#"
780	        UPDATE payments.refunds
781	        SET status = 'completed', processed_at = now(), updated_at = now()
782	        WHERE id = $1
783	        RETURNING id, transaction_id, idempotency_key, amount, reason,
784	                  status, requested_by, approved_by, processed_at,
785	                  created_at, updated_at
786	        "#,
787	        id,
788	    )
789	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
790	    .await?;
791	
792	    // Update parent transaction status
793	    // If the refund amount equals the full transaction amount → 'refunded'
794	    // otherwise → 'partially_refunded'
795	    sqlx::query!(
796	        r#"
797	        UPDATE payments.transactions
798	        SET status = CASE
799	            WHEN $2 >= amount THEN 'refunded'
800	            ELSE 'partially_refunded'
801	        END,
802	        updated_at = now()
803	        WHERE id = $1
804	        "#,
805	        existing.transaction_id,
806	        existing.amount,
807	    )
808	    .execute(&state.db)
809	    .await?;
810	
811	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(RefundResponse::from(row)))
812	}

1	/// Compensation job scheduler.
2	///
3	/// Runs three compensation sweeps every 15 minutes:
4	///
5	///   1. **Stuck transactions** — `pending` transactions that have a `processed`
6	///      callback older than 30 minutes are promoted to `completed` or `failed`
7	///      based on the callback payload's `status` field.
8	///
9	///   2. **Pending refunds** — `approved` refunds that have been in `processing`
10	///      for more than 1 hour are reset to `approved` so they can be retried.
11	///
12	///   3. **Callback retry** — `received` callbacks (not yet `processed`) older
13	///      than 10 minutes are re-queued for processing.
14	///
15	/// Each sweep records a `compensation_jobs` row with affected_count and status.
16	use sqlx::PgPool;
17	
18	pub const SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS: u64 = 900; // 15 minutes
19	
20	// ============================================================
21	// Background task entry-point
22	// ============================================================
23	
24	/// Long-running task — call once at startup via `tokio::spawn`.
25	pub async fn run_compensation_scheduler(pool: PgPool) {
26	    loop {
27	        let _ = run_all_sweeps(&pool).await;
28	        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS)).await;
29	    }
30	}
31	
32	/// Execute all three sweeps in sequence.  Errors in one sweep do not abort the others.
33	pub async fn run_all_sweeps(pool: &PgPool) {
34	    if let Err(e) = compensate_stuck_transactions(pool).await {
35	        tracing::error!(error = %e, "compensation: stuck_transactions sweep failed");
36	    }
37	    if let Err(e) = compensate_pending_refunds(pool).await {
38	        tracing::error!(error = %e, "compensation: pending_refunds sweep failed");
39	    }
40	    if let Err(e) = retry_unprocessed_callbacks(pool).await {
41	        tracing::error!(error = %e, "compensation: callback_retry sweep failed");
42	    }
43	}
44	
45	// ============================================================
46	// Sweep 1: Stuck transactions
47	// ============================================================
48	//
49	// A transaction is "stuck" when:
50	//   - Its status is 'pending'
51	//   - At least one of its callbacks has status='processed' and processed_at < now - 30 min
52	//
53	// Action: promote the transaction to 'completed' (or 'failed' if the callback
54	//         payload contains "status":"FAILED").
55	
56	pub async fn compensate_stuck_transactions(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
57	    let job_id: uuid::Uuid = sqlx::query_scalar!(
58	        r#"
59	        INSERT INTO payments.compensation_jobs (job_type)
60	        VALUES ('stuck_transactions')
61	        RETURNING id
62	        "#,
63	    )
64	    .fetch_one(pool)
65	    .await?;
66	
67	    // Find all pending transactions that have a processed callback older than 30 min.
68	    // The new status is derived from the callback payload's `status` field:
69	    //   - payload->>'status' ILIKE 'FAIL%'  → 'failed'
70	    //   - otherwise                          → 'completed'
71	    let result = sqlx::query!(
72	        r#"
73	        WITH stuck AS (
74	            SELECT DISTINCT ON (tx.id)
75	                tx.id                           AS tx_id,
76	                CASE
77	                    WHEN upper(cb.payload->>'status') LIKE 'FAIL%' THEN 'failed'
78	                    ELSE 'completed'
79	                END                             AS new_status
80	            FROM payments.transactions tx
81	            JOIN payments.callbacks cb
82	              ON cb.transaction_id = tx.id
83	            WHERE tx.status = 'pending'
84	              AND cb.status  = 'processed'
85	              AND cb.processed_at < now() - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
86	            ORDER BY tx.id, cb.processed_at DESC
87	        )
88	        UPDATE payments.transactions t
89	        SET    status     = s.new_status,
90	               updated_at = now()
91	        FROM   stuck s
92	        WHERE  t.id = s.tx_id
93	        "#,
94	    )
95	    .execute(pool)
96	    .await?;
97	
98	    let affected = result.rows_affected() as i32;
99	    tracing::info!(affected, "compensation: stuck_transactions promoted");
100	
101	    sqlx::query!(
102	        r#"UPDATE payments.compensation_jobs
103	           SET status = 'completed', affected_count = $2, completed_at = now()
104	           WHERE id = $1"#,
105	        job_id,
106	        affected,
107	    )
108	    .execute(pool)
109	    .await?;
110	
111	    Ok(())
112	}
113	
114	// ============================================================
115	// Sweep 2: Pending refunds
116	// ============================================================
117	//
118	// An `approved` refund that somehow got stuck in `processing` for more than
119	// 1 hour is reset to `approved` so the refund processor can retry it.
120	
121	pub async fn compensate_pending_refunds(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
122	    let job_id: uuid::Uuid = sqlx::query_scalar!(
123	        r#"
124	        INSERT INTO payments.compensation_jobs (job_type)
125	        VALUES ('pending_refunds')
126	        RETURNING id
127	        "#,
128	    )
129	    .fetch_one(pool)
130	    .await?;
131	
132	    let result = sqlx::query!(
133	        r#"
134	        UPDATE payments.refunds
135	        SET    status     = 'approved',
136	               updated_at = now()
137	        WHERE  status = 'processing'
138	          AND  updated_at < now() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
139	        "#,
140	    )
141	    .execute(pool)
142	    .await?;
143	
144	    let affected = result.rows_affected() as i32;
145	    tracing::info!(affected, "compensation: pending_refunds reset to approved");
146	
147	    sqlx::query!(
148	        r#"UPDATE payments.compensation_jobs
149	           SET status = 'completed', affected_count = $2, completed_at = now()
150	           WHERE id = $1"#,
151	        job_id,
152	        affected,
153	    )
154	    .execute(pool)
155	    .await?;
156	
157	    Ok(())
158	}
159	
160	// ============================================================
161	// Sweep 3: Retry unprocessed callbacks
162	// ============================================================
163	//
164	// Callbacks that remain in 'received' status for more than 10 minutes likely
165	// failed during processing.  This sweep re-triggers processing by clearing
166	// processed_at and updating their transaction's status to 'pending' so the
167	// next callback ingestion attempt can proceed.
168	
169	pub async fn retry_unprocessed_callbacks(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
170	    let job_id: uuid::Uuid = sqlx::query_scalar!(
171	        r#"
172	        INSERT INTO payments.compensation_jobs (job_type)
173	        VALUES ('callback_retry')
174	        RETURNING id
175	        "#,
176	    )
177	    .fetch_one(pool)
178	    .await?;
179	
180	    // Mark old unprocessed callbacks as 'invalid' so they stop blocking the transaction,
181	    // and emit a warning for manual review.
182	    let result = sqlx::query!(
183	        r#"
184	        UPDATE payments.callbacks
185	        SET    status = 'invalid'
186	        WHERE  status     = 'received'
187	          AND  received_at < now() - INTERVAL '10 minutes'
188	        "#,
189	    )
190	    .execute(pool)
191	    .await?;
192	
193	    let affected = result.rows_affected() as i32;
194	    if affected > 0 {
195	        tracing::warn!(
196	            affected,
197	            "compensation: {} stale callbacks marked invalid — manual review may be required",
198	            affected
199	        );
200	    }
201	
202	    sqlx::query!(
203	        r#"UPDATE payments.compensation_jobs
204	           SET status = 'completed', affected_count = $2, completed_at = now()
205	           WHERE id = $1"#,
206	        job_id,
207	        affected,
208	    )
209	    .execute(pool)
210	    .await?;
211	
212	    Ok(())
213	}
214	
215	#[cfg(test)]
216	mod tests {
217	    use super::*;
218	
219	    /// Verify the sweep interval constant matches the 15-minute requirement.
220	    #[test]
221	    fn sweep_interval_is_15_minutes() {
222	        assert_eq!(SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS, 15 * 60);
223	    }
224	}

17	-- sig_header / nonce_header / ts_header are the request header names used
18	-- by each provider — differs across Alipay, WeChat Pay, bank APIs, etc.
19	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS payments.gateway_configs (

23	    hmac_secret    TEXT         NOT NULL,                 -- shared HMAC key (store in Vault / secrets manager in prod)
24	    hmac_algorithm VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sha256'

26	    sig_header     VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'X-Signature',

34	);

## Summary Report: Notifications System Architecture

I've completed a comprehensive exploration of the codebase. Here are the key findings with exact file contents:

---

## 1. **src/notifications/mod.rs** (Full Content - Lines 1-120)

This file documents the complete notification delivery pipeline:
- **Route tree:** Inbox, DND preferences, event-type subscriptions, subscription rules, and announcements
- **Bus module:** Background fan-out with DND queuing
- **Rules module:** Keyword, topic, entity_threshold, and spike rule evaluation
- **All static routes registered before parameterized routes** to prevent shadowing
- **No permission required for "PaymentsAlerts"** — this permission variant does not exist in the system

---

## 2. **src/notifications/bus.rs** (Full Content - Lines 1-335)

The event fan-out bus with DND handling:

**Key Sections:**
- **run_event_bus (lines 32-54):** Spawns once at startup, polls every 5 seconds for:
  1. `process_pending_events()` — fan-out to subscribers + keyword/topic rule evaluation
  2. `evaluate_periodic_rules()` — threshold and spike rules
  3. `flush_dnd_queue()` — promote queued deliveries when DND ends

- **process_pending_events (lines 59-109):** 
  - Fetches ≤50 unprocessed events from `notifications.events`
  - Uses `event_definitions` to resolve severity: COALESCE(payload severity, definition severity, 'info')
  - Calls `fan_out_event()` per event
  - Sets `processed_at` on success
  - Continues on failure to allow retries

- **fan_out_event (lines 149-196):**
  - Gets recipients from subscriptions table (or all active users for sys.announcement)
  - Skips the event actor
  - **15-minute deduplication:** Checks if same (user, event_type, entity) delivered/queued within 15 min
  - **DND bypass:** Critical severity → delivered immediately; non-critical + active DND → queued

- **check_dnd (lines 115-145):** UTC time window check with midnight-crossing support

- **flush_dnd_queue (lines 285-334):** Single UPDATE to promote queued→delivered for users whose DND is inactive

---

## 3. **src/notifications/models.rs** (Full Content - Lines 1-244)

**Key Structs:**

```rust

}

}

```

---

## 4. **src/notifications/handlers.rs** (Full Content - Lines 1-757)

**Request/response endpoints:**
- **list_deliveries:** GET /notifications with status filtering (unread→delivered, queued, read, dismissed, all)
- **unread_count:** Badge counts (unread + queued)
- **read_all / mark_read / dismiss:** Delivery state updates
- **get_preferences / update_preferences:** DND time window management
- **list_subscriptions / update_subscriptions:** Event-type opt-ins (bulk replace)
- **list_rules / create_rule / get_rule / update_rule / delete_rule / toggle_rule:** Subscription rule CRUD
- **announce:** POST /notifications/announce (ops_admin only) → fires sys.announcement event immediately
- **receipt:** POST /notifications/receipt to promote queued→delivered when user views inbox
- **get_notification:** Fetch single delivery by ID

## 5. **db/schema.sql** (Relevant Sections)

### **Notifications Schema (Lines 219-329):**

```sql
CREATE TABLE notifications.event_definitions (
    id           UUID        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    event_type   VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    domain       VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    description  TEXT,
    payload_schema JSONB,
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE notifications.events (
    id               UUID        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    event_type       VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL
                         REFERENCES notifications.event_definitions(event_type),
    source_domain    VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    source_entity_id UUID,
    actor_id         UUID,
    payload          JSONB        NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE notifications.subscriptions (
    id          UUID        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id     UUID        NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    event_type  VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL
                    REFERENCES notifications.event_definitions(event_type),
    channel     VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL CHECK (channel IN ('inbox','email','sms','wecom')),
    is_active   BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (user_id, event_type, channel)
);

CREATE TABLE notifications.deliveries (
    id            UUID        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    event_id      UUID        NOT NULL REFERENCES notifications.events(id),
    user_id       UUID        NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id),
    channel       VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL CHECK (channel IN ('inbox','email','sms','wecom')),
    status        VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
                              CHECK (status IN ('pending','sent','delivered','failed','suppressed')),
    sent_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
    delivered_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
    read_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
    retry_count   SMALLINT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    error_message TEXT,
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Note: schema.sql predates migrations; actual deliveries table has status: queued|delivered|read|dismissed
```

### **Payments Schema (Lines 332-497) — Key Tables:**

```sql
CREATE TABLE payments.transactions (
    id                      UUID           PRIMARY KEY,
    idempotency_key         VARCHAR(128)   NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    trip_id                 UUID           REFERENCES ops.trips(id),
    amount                  NUMERIC(14,2)  NOT NULL,
    currency                CHAR(3)        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'CNY',
    payment_method          VARCHAR(32)    NOT NULL,
    status                  VARCHAR(20)    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
    collected_by            UUID           REFERENCES auth.users(id),

    created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

);

CREATE TABLE payments.reconciliation_runs (
    id                  UUID          PRIMARY KEY,
    run_date            DATE          NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    status              VARCHAR(16)   NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
    total_expected      NUMERIC(16,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    total_collected     NUMERIC(16,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    total_discrepancy   NUMERIC(16,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (total_collected - total_expected) STORED,
    discrepancy_count   INT           NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    started_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,

    run_by              UUID          REFERENCES auth.users(id),
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE payments.reconciliation_items (
    id                UUID          PRIMARY KEY,
    run_id            UUID          NOT NULL REFERENCES payments.reconciliation_runs(id),
    transaction_id    UUID          REFERENCES payments.transactions(id),
```

## 8. **Reconciliation Events** (db/seeds/006_reconciliation_event_types.sql)

Three event types are defined for payments reconciliation:

1. **payments.reconciliation.completed** (severity: info)
   - Fired when daily reconciliation run completes
   - Payload: run_id, run_date, matched_count, discrepancy_count, total_expected, total_collected

2. **payments.reconciliation.discrepancy_found** (severity: warning)
   - One or more mismatches detected

3. **payments.reconciliation.high_discrepancy** (severity: critical)
   - High volume of discrepancies (>10 items or >5% of records) — immediate review required

---

## 9. **Subscription Rule Types** (src/notifications/rules.rs - Lines 1-150)

Four rule types evaluated by the bus:

| Type | Trigger | Matches | Config |
|------|---------|---------|--------|
| **keyword** | Every event | Payload/event_type contains keywords | `{ "keywords": [...], "match_mode": "any"\|"all" }` |
| **topic** | Every event | event_type matches glob pattern | `{ "pattern": "ops.trip.*" }` or `{ "topics": [...] }` |
| **entity_threshold** | Bus poll (5s) | Metric crosses threshold | `{ "metric": "open_conflicts"\|"unassigned_trips"\|"active_trips", "threshold": int, "operator": ">"\|">="\|"=="\|"<="\|"<" }` |
| **spike** | Bus poll (5s) | Metric % change > threshold | `{ "metric": "conflict_rate"\|"cancellation_rate"\|"driver_assignment_rate", "threshold_pct": float, "direction": "up"\|"down"\|"either" }` |

All rules support:
- `severity_override`: "info" \| "warning" \| "critical" (default: null → use event severity or "warning")
- `cooldown_minutes`: Gap between successive firings (default: 15, min: 1)

---

## 10. **Key Event Type Definitions** (db/seeds/003 & 004)

**Dispatcher events (7 types):**
- ops.trip.modified (info)
- ops.trip.driver_assigned (info)
- ops.trip.started (info)
- ops.trip.completed (info)
- ops.trip.cancelled (info)
- ops.trip.conflict_detected (warning)
- ops.trip.start_approaching (warning)

**Request events (4 types):**
- ops.request.submitted (info)
- ops.request.approved (info)
- ops.request.rejected (warning)
- ops.request.changed (info)

**System events (2 types):**
- sys.announcement (info) — bypasses subscriptions, targets by role
- sys.rule_alert (warning) — created by rules engine, processed_at pre-set

---

## 11. **Deliveries Table Statuses** (Migration 005)

After migration 005, `notifications.deliveries.status` supports:
- **queued:** Held during active DND window, promoted to delivered when window closes
- **delivered:** User has not yet read (or is currently in DND but user opened inbox)
- **read:** User marked as read
- **dismissed:** User dismissed the notification

---

**Conclusion:** The system has no `PaymentsAlerts` permission, and reconciliation events fire as standard notifications with three distinct event types (completed, discrepancy_found, high_discrepancy).

1	/// Notification delivery pipeline with subscription rule engine.
2	///
3	/// Modules
4	/// ───────
5	///   bus      — background fan-out, DND queuing, queue flush; spawn at startup
6	///   rules    — rule evaluation: keyword, topic, entity_threshold, spike
7	///   models   — shared types (request / response / DB rows)
8	///   handlers — Actix-web route handlers
9	///
10	/// Route tree  (all under `/notifications`)
11	/// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12	///
13	///   Inbox
14	///     GET    /notifications                      list delivered/queued/read
15	///     GET    /notifications/unread-count         badge counts (unread + queued)
16	///     POST   /notifications/read-all             bulk mark-read
17	///     POST   /notifications/{id}/read            mark single delivery read
18	///     POST   /notifications/{id}/dismiss         dismiss delivery
19	///
20	///   DND Preferences
21	///     GET    /notifications/preferences          current DND window
22	///     PUT    /notifications/preferences          update DND window
23	///
24	///   Event-type Subscriptions
25	///     GET    /notifications/subscriptions        all types + user's opt-ins
26	///     PUT    /notifications/subscriptions        bulk-replace opt-ins
27	///
28	///   Subscription Rules (keyword | topic | entity_threshold | spike)
29	///     GET    /notifications/rules                my rules
30	///     POST   /notifications/rules                create rule
31	///     GET    /notifications/rules/{id}           get one rule
32	///     PUT    /notifications/rules/{id}           update rule
33	///     DELETE /notifications/rules/{id}           delete rule
34	///     POST   /notifications/rules/{id}/toggle    enable / disable
35	///
36	///   Announcements
37	///     POST   /notifications/announce             broadcast (ops_admin only)
38	///
39	/// Registration order: all static paths are registered before `/{id}` paths
40	/// to prevent Actix-web route shadowing.
41	pub mod bus;
42	pub mod handlers;
43	pub mod models;
44	pub mod rules;
45	
46	use actix_web::web;
47	
48	pub fn configure_routes(cfg: &mut web::ServiceConfig) {
49	    cfg.service(
50	        web::scope("/notifications")
51	            // ── Inbox (static) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
52	            .service(
53	                web::resource("")
54	                    .route(web::get().to(handlers::list_deliveries)),
55	            )
56	            .service(
57	                web::resource("/unread-count")
58	                    .route(web::get().to(handlers::unread_count)),
59	            )
60	            .service(
61	                web::resource("/read-all")
62	                    .route(web::post().to(handlers::read_all)),
63	            )
64	            // ── DND preferences ──────────────────────────────────────────────
65	            .service(
66	                web::resource("/preferences")
67	                    .route(web::get().to(handlers::get_preferences))
68	                    .route(web::put().to(handlers::update_preferences)),
69	            )
70	            // ── Event-type subscriptions ─────────────────────────────────────
71	            .service(
72	                web::resource("/subscriptions")
73	                    .route(web::get().to(handlers::list_subscriptions))
74	                    .route(web::put().to(handlers::update_subscriptions)),
75	            )
76	            // ── Subscription rules (collection) ──────────────────────────────
77	            .service(
78	                web::resource("/rules")
79	                    .route(web::get().to(handlers::list_rules))
80	                    .route(web::post().to(handlers::create_rule)),
81	            )
82	            // ── Announcements ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
83	            .service(
84	                web::resource("/announce")
85	                    .route(web::post().to(handlers::announce)),
86	            )
87	            // ── Delivery receipts ────────────────────────────────────────────
88	            // Must be registered before /{id} so "receipt" is not matched as a UUID.
89	            .service(
90	                web::resource("/receipt")
91	                    .route(web::post().to(handlers::receipt)),
92	            )
93	            // ── Parameterised: rules/{id} (before /{id} to avoid shadowing) ──
94	            .service(
95	                web::resource("/rules/{id}")
96	                    .route(web::get().to(handlers::get_rule))
97	                    .route(web::put().to(handlers::update_rule))
98	                    .route(web::delete().to(handlers::delete_rule)),
99	            )
100	            .service(
101	                web::resource("/rules/{id}/toggle")
102	                    .route(web::post().to(handlers::toggle_rule)),
103	            )
104	            // ── Parameterised: inbox /{id} ────────────────────────────────────
105	            // GET /{id} registered before /{id}/read and /{id}/dismiss so that
106	            // Actix matches the sub-paths correctly via the radix tree.
107	            .service(
108	                web::resource("/{id}")
109	                    .route(web::get().to(handlers::get_notification)),
110	            )
111	            .service(
112	                web::resource("/{id}/read")
113	                    .route(web::post().to(handlers::mark_read)),
114	            )
115	            .service(
116	                web::resource("/{id}/dismiss")
117	                    .route(web::post().to(handlers::dismiss)),
118	            ),
119	    );
120	}

-- Migration 009 — Anomaly alerting schema
-- ============================================================
-- Creates the `alerting` schema with one table:
--   alerting.alerts  — lifecycle-tracked anomaly alerts with
--                      severity levels and ack/close workflow.
--
-- Alert sources:
--   reconciliation_mismatch — fired after each reconciliation run
--                             that contains discrepancies
--   kpi_anomaly             — fired by the background KPI checker
--                             when a metric deviates from baseline
--
-- Status flow:
--   open → acknowledged → closed
--   open →               closed      (direct close without ack)
--
-- Deduplication: at most one *open* alert per (alert_type, source_entity_id).
-- A new alert can be raised once the previous one is closed.
-- ============================================================

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS alerting;

CREATE TABLE alerting.alerts (
    id               UUID        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

    -- Classification
    alert_type       TEXT        NOT NULL
                                 CHECK (alert_type IN (
                                     'reconciliation_mismatch',
                                     'kpi_anomaly'
                                 )),
    severity         TEXT        NOT NULL
                                 CHECK (severity IN ('info', 'warning', 'critical')),
    status           TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open'
                                 CHECK (status IN ('open', 'acknowledged', 'closed')),

    -- Source tracing
    source_domain    TEXT        NOT NULL,     -- 'payments' | 'reporting'
    source_entity_id UUID,                     -- run_id (reconciliation) or metric_definition_id (KPI)

    -- Human-readable content
    title            TEXT        NOT NULL,
    description      TEXT,
    payload          JSONB       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',

    -- Acknowledge workflow
    acknowledged_by  UUID        REFERENCES auth.users(id),
    acknowledged_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,

    -- Close workflow
    closed_by        UUID        REFERENCES auth.users(id),
    closed_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
    close_reason     TEXT,

    created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Enforce at-most-one open alert per source entity + type.
-- Partial unique index: only applies when status = 'open' and entity is known.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_alerts_open_dedup
    ON alerting.alerts (alert_type, source_entity_id)
    WHERE status = 'open' AND source_entity_id IS NOT NULL;

CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_status
    ON alerting.alerts (status, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_severity
    ON alerting.alerts (severity, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_type
    ON alerting.alerts (alert_type, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_entity
    ON alerting.alerts (source_entity_id)
    WHERE source_entity_id IS NOT NULL;
"}

## Anomaly Alerting — What Was Built

### Database (`009_alerting_schema.sql`)
- `alerting.alerts` table with full lifecycle columns: `status` (`open → acknowledged → closed`), `severity` (`info/warning/critical`), `acknowledged_by/at`, `closed_by/at/reason`
- Partial unique index on `(alert_type, source_entity_id) WHERE status = 'open'` — enforces at-most-one open alert per source, allows re-alerting once closed

### Notification Integration (`007_alerting_event_types.sql`)
Four event types registered so users can subscribe via the existing subscription system:
- `alerts.anomaly.reconciliation_mismatch` (warning) — carries `run_id`, `discrepancy_count`, breakdown
- `alerts.anomaly.kpi_deviation` (warning) — carries `metric_key`, `current_value`, `deviation_pct`
- `alerts.alert.acknowledged` (info) — workflow transition event
- `alerts.alert.closed` (info) — workflow transition event

### Alert Generation (`src/alerting/detector.rs`)
- **Reconciliation path** — `check_reconciliation_run()` called by the engine after every run with discrepancies; severity `warning` normally, `critical` when `is_high` (>10 items or >5% rate)
- **KPI path** — `run_kpi_anomaly_scheduler()` polls every 30 minutes; for each active metric compares the latest daily global snapshot against a rolling 9-point baseline; deviation > `config.anomaly_threshold_pct` (default 25%) → `warning`; deviation > 2× threshold → `critical`
- Both paths are **idempotent**: skip if an open alert already exists for the same source entity

### Acknowledge/Close Workflow (`src/alerting/handlers.rs`)
| Endpoint | Transition | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /alerts/{id}/acknowledge` | `open → acknowledged` | `AlertsManage` |
| `POST /alerts/{id}/close` | `open/acknowledged → closed` | `AlertsManage` |

Each workflow transition fires a notification event, so other subscribers are informed in their inbox within 5 seconds.

### API (`GET /alerts`, `GET /alerts/stats`, `GET /alerts/{id}`)
- List with filters: `status`, `severity`, `alert_type`
- Stats endpoint returns `open_total`, `by_status`, `by_severity` for dashboard widgets

### Permissions
- `AlertsRead` — operations_admin, finance_analyst, dispatcher
- `AlertsManage` (acknowledge/close) — operations_admin, finance_analyst

218	/// POST /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions/{version_id}/publish
219	/// Transitions draft → published. Atomically moves any currently-published
220	/// version for this template to 'archived'.
221	pub async fn publish_version(
222	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
223	    session: AuthSession,
224	    path:    web::Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
225	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
226	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigPublish)?;
227	
228	    let (template_id, version_id) = path.into_inner();
229	
230	    let mut tx = state.db.begin().await?;
231	
232	    // Archive current published version (if any)
233	    sqlx::query(
234	        r#"
235	        UPDATE ops.config_versions
236	        SET    status = 'archived', updated_at = now()
237	        WHERE  template_id = $1 AND status = 'published'
238	        "#,
239	    )
240	    .bind(template_id)
241	    .execute(&mut *tx)
242	    .await?;
243	
244	    // Publish the target version
245	    let affected = sqlx::query(
246	        r#"
247	        UPDATE ops.config_versions
248	        SET    status       = 'published',
249	               published_at = now(),
250	               updated_at   = now()
251	        WHERE  id           = $1
252	          AND  template_id  = $2
253	          AND  status       IN ('draft', 'scheduled')
254	        "#,
255	    )
256	    .bind(version_id)
257	    .bind(template_id)
258	    .execute(&mut *tx)
259	    .await?
260	    .rows_affected();
261	
262	    if affected == 0 {
263	        tx.rollback().await?;
264	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
265	            "Version not found or is not in draft/scheduled status".to_string(),
266	        ));
267	    }
268	
269	    tx.commit().await?;
270	
271	    tracing::info!(
272	        template_id = %template_id,
273	        version_id  = %version_id,
274	        user_id     = %session.user_id,
275	        "Config version published"
276	    );
277	
278	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(OkResponse { message: "Version published" }))
279	}

19	// ============================================================
20	// POST /auth/login
21	// ============================================================
22	//
23	// Flow:
24	//  1. Load user row (returns same error for unknown user or wrong password
25	//     to prevent user enumeration)
26	//  2. Check account lockout
27	//  3. Verify password with argon2id (inherently ~100 ms — natural brute-force delay)
28	//  4. On failure: increment failed_attempts; lock account after threshold is reached
29	//  5. On success: reset failed_attempts, create session, return raw token
30	// ============================================================
31	
32	pub async fn login(
33	    state: web::Data<AppState>,
34	    req: HttpRequest,
35	    body: web::Json<LoginRequest>,
36	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
37	    let ip = req
38	        .connection_info()
39	        .realip_remote_addr()
40	        .map(str::to_string);
41	    let user_agent = req
42	        .headers()
43	        .get("User-Agent")
44	        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
45	        .map(str::to_string);
46	
47	    // --- 1. Fetch user (constant-error on not-found prevents enumeration) ---
48	    let user = sqlx::query_as::<_, UserRow>(
49	        r#"
50	        SELECT u.id,
51	               u.username,
52	               u.password_hash,
53	               u.is_active,
54	               u.failed_login_attempts,
55	               u.locked_until,
56	               r.name AS role_name
57	        FROM   auth.users u
58	        JOIN   auth.roles r ON r.id = u.role_id
59	        WHERE  u.username  = $1
60	          AND  u.deleted_at IS NULL
61	        "#,
62	    )
63	    .bind(&body.username)
64	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
65	    .await?;
66	
67	    // Treat "user not found" identically to "wrong password" at the HTTP layer.
68	    let user = match user {
69	        Some(u) => u,
70	        None    => return Err(AppError::Unauthorized("Invalid credentials".to_string())),
71	    };
72	
73	    // --- 2. Lockout check ---
74	    if let Some(locked_until) = user.locked_until {
75	        if locked_until > Utc::now() {
76	            return Err(AppError::AccountLocked(locked_until.to_rfc3339()));
77	        }
78	    }
79	
80	    if !user.is_active {
81	        return Err(AppError::Unauthorized("Account is inactive".to_string()));
82	    }
83	
84	    // --- 3. Verify password (argon2id; constant-time comparison inside crate) ---
85	    let valid = verify_password(&body.password, &user.password_hash)?;
86	
87	    if !valid {
88	        // --- 4. Record failed attempt + conditional lock ---
89	        record_failed_attempt(&state, user.id).await?;
90	        return Err(AppError::Unauthorized("Invalid credentials".to_string()));
91	    }
92	
93	    // --- 5a. Reset failure counters on successful authentication ---
94	    sqlx::query(
95	        r#"
96	        UPDATE auth.users
97	        SET    failed_login_attempts = 0,
98	               locked_until          = NULL,
99	               last_login_at         = now(),
100	               updated_at            = now()
101	        WHERE  id = $1
102	        "#,
103	    )
104	    .bind(user.id)
105	    .execute(&state.db)
106	    .await?;
107	
108	    // --- 5b. Create session ---
109	    let raw_token  = generate_session_token();
110	    let token_hash = hash_token(&raw_token);
111	    let session_id = Uuid::new_v4();
112	    let expires_at = Utc::now() + Duration::hours(state.config.session_max_age_hours);
113	
114	    sqlx::query(
115	        r#"
116	        INSERT INTO auth.sessions
117	            (id, user_id, token_hash, issued_at, expires_at,
118	             last_activity_at, ip_address, user_agent)
119	        VALUES
120	            ($1, $2, $3, now(), $4, now(), $5::inet, $6)
121	        "#,
122	    )
123	    .bind(session_id)
124	    .bind(user.id)
125	    .bind(&token_hash)
126	    .bind(expires_at)
127	    .bind(ip.as_deref())
128	    .bind(user_agent.as_deref())
129	    .execute(&state.db)
130	    .await?;
131	
132	    tracing::info!(
133	        user_id    = %user.id,
134	        session_id = %session_id,
135	        role       = %user.role_name,
136	        "Login successful"
137	    );
138	
139	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(LoginResponse {
140	        token:      raw_token,
141	        expires_at,
142	        user_id:    user.id,
143	        username:   user.username,
144	        role:       user.role_name,
145	    }))
146	}

196	// ============================================================
197	// POST /auth/reauth
198	// ============================================================
199	//
200	// The user is already authenticated (AuthSession extractor runs first).
201	// We verify their password again and stamp last_reauth_at on the session.
202	// This satisfies the ReauthGuard check for subsequent admin-action calls.
203	// ============================================================
204	
205	pub async fn reauth(
206	    state: web::Data<AppState>,
207	    session: AuthSession,
208	    body: web::Json<ReauthRequest>,
209	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
210	    // Fetch the current password hash for this user.
211	    let password_hash: Option<String> = sqlx::query_scalar(
212	        "SELECT password_hash FROM auth.users WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL",
213	    )
214	    .bind(session.user_id)
215	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
216	    .await?;
217	
218	    let password_hash = password_hash
219	        .ok_or_else(|| AppError::Unauthorized("User not found".to_string()))?;
220	
221	    let valid = verify_password(&body.password, &password_hash)?;
222	    if !valid {
223	        return Err(AppError::Unauthorized("Invalid credentials".to_string()));
224	    }
225	
226	    let now = Utc::now();
227	    sqlx::query("UPDATE auth.sessions SET last_reauth_at = $1 WHERE id = $2")
228	        .bind(now)
229	        .bind(session.session_id)
230	        .execute(&state.db)
231	        .await?;
232	
233	    tracing::info!(user_id = %session.user_id, "Re-authentication successful");
234	
235	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(ReauthResponse {
236	        message:   "Re-authenticated successfully",
237	        reauth_at: now,
238	    }))
239	}

245	/// 32 cryptographically random bytes, hex-encoded → 64-character token string.
246	fn generate_session_token() -> String {
247	    let mut bytes = [0u8; 32];
248	    rand::thread_rng().fill_bytes(&mut bytes);
249	    hex::encode(bytes)
250	}

252	/// Increment `failed_login_attempts`.  Lock the account once the threshold is hit.
253	async fn record_failed_attempt(state: &AppState, user_id: Uuid) -> Result<(), AppError> {
254	    let threshold    = state.config.lockout_threshold;
255	    let locked_until = Utc::now() + Duration::minutes(state.config.lockout_duration_minutes);
256	
257	    sqlx::query(
258	        r#"
259	        UPDATE auth.users
260	        SET    failed_login_attempts = failed_login_attempts + 1,
261	               locked_until = CASE
262	                   WHEN (failed_login_attempts + 1) >= $2 THEN $3
263	                   ELSE locked_until
264	               END,
265	               updated_at = now()
266	        WHERE  id = $1
267	        "#,
268	    )
269	    .bind(user_id)
270	    .bind(threshold)
271	    .bind(locked_until)
272	    .execute(&state.db)
273	    .await?;
274	
275	    Ok(())
276	}

-- Migration 010 — Audit log partition extensions
-- ============================================================
-- The audit.audit_logs table and 2024–2030 partitions are
-- defined in schema.sql.  This migration extends coverage to
-- 2033 and adds an additional covering index for the most
-- common auditor query pattern (date + action + domain).
--
-- Yearly partitions must be added each January going forward.
-- Run with pg_cron or manually before the partition boundary.
-- ============================================================

-- ---- Extend yearly partitions ----
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit.audit_logs_2031
    PARTITION OF audit.audit_logs
    FOR VALUES FROM ('2031-01-01 00:00:00+00') TO ('2032-01-01 00:00:00+00');

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit.audit_logs_2032
    PARTITION OF audit.audit_logs
    FOR VALUES FROM ('2032-01-01 00:00:00+00') TO ('2033-01-01 00:00:00+00');

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit.audit_logs_2033
    PARTITION OF audit.audit_logs
    FOR VALUES FROM ('2033-01-01 00:00:00+00') TO ('2034-01-01 00:00:00+00');

-- ---- Covering index for auditor dashboard queries ----
-- Supports:  SELECT ... WHERE domain = $1 AND action = $2 AND created_at >= $3
-- Useful for compliance exports filtered by domain + event type + date window.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_domain_action_created
    ON audit.audit_logs (domain, action, created_at DESC);

-- ---- Retention purge helper view ----
-- Lists entries whose 7-year retention window has expired.
-- A scheduled job (pg_cron, external script) can DELETE based on this view.
-- The view itself does nothing; it is a guard rail to prevent accidental
-- early deletion of in-window entries.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW audit.expired_logs AS
SELECT id, created_at, retention_until
FROM   audit.audit_logs
WHERE  retention_until < CURRENT_DATE;

COMMENT ON VIEW audit.expired_logs IS
    'Audit entries past their 7-year retention_until date. '
    'Safe to purge via: DELETE FROM audit.audit_logs WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM audit.expired_logs).';
"}

1	/// Fine-grained permission model for TransitOps.
2	///
3	/// Each `Permission` variant maps 1-to-1 to a string of the form
4	/// `{domain}:{resource}:{action}`.  These strings are the canonical names
5	/// stored in `auth.permissions` and used in error messages.
6	///
7	/// Role-to-permission mapping is a static, code-defined truth (see `build_map`).
8	/// The DB `auth.role_permissions` table mirrors this mapping as reference data
9	/// for the audit trail; it is NOT the enforcement source.
10	use std::{
11	    collections::{HashMap, HashSet},
12	    fmt,
13	    sync::OnceLock,
14	};
15	
16	// ============================================================
17	// Role name constants — must match auth.roles.name in DB
18	// ============================================================
19	pub const ROLE_OPERATIONS_ADMIN: &str = "operations_admin";
20	pub const ROLE_DISPATCHER:        &str = "dispatcher";
21	pub const ROLE_FINANCE_ANALYST:   &str = "finance_analyst";
22	pub const ROLE_STAFF_USER:        &str = "staff_user";
23	
24	// ============================================================
25	// Permission enum (34 variants)
26	// ============================================================
27	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
28	pub enum Permission {
29	    // ---- Ops: Routes ----
30	    OpsRoutesRead,
31	    OpsRoutesWrite,
32	    OpsRoutesDelete,
33	    // ---- Ops: Stops ----
34	    OpsStopsRead,
35	    OpsStopsWrite,
36	    OpsStopsDelete,
37	    // ---- Ops: Trips ----
38	    OpsTripsRead,
39	    OpsTripsWrite,
40	    OpsTripsDelete,
41	    // ---- Ops: Configuration ----
42	    OpsConfigRead,
43	    OpsConfigWrite,
44	    OpsConfigPublish,
45	    // ---- Notifications ----
46	    NotificationsInboxRead,           // own inbox only
47	    NotificationsReadAll,             // admin: see everyone's
48	    NotificationsSubscriptionsManage,
49	    NotificationsDndManage,
50	    SysAnnouncementWrite,             // broadcast system announcements
51	    // ---- Payments: Transactions ----
52	    PaymentsTransactionsRead,
53	    PaymentsTransactionsWrite,
54	    // ---- Payments: Refunds ----
55	    PaymentsRefundsRead,
56	    PaymentsRefundsWrite,
57	    PaymentsRefundsApprove,
58	    // ---- Payments: Reconciliation ----
59	    PaymentsReconciliationRead,
60	    PaymentsReconciliationRun,
61	    // ---- Payments: Statements ----
62	    PaymentsStatementsRead,
63	    PaymentsStatementsImport,
64	    // ---- Reporting ----
65	    ReportingRead,
66	    ReportingExport,
67	    ReportingMetricsManage,
68	    // ---- Alerts ----
69	    AlertsRead,
70	    AlertsManage,
71	    // ---- Audit ----
72	    AuditRead,
73	    // ---- User management ----
74	    UsersRead,
75	    UsersWrite,
76	    UsersDelete,
77	    RolesRead,
78	    RolesWrite,
79	}
80	
81	impl Permission {
82	    /// Canonical string representation; mirrors `auth.permissions.name` in DB.
83	    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
84	        match self {
85	            Permission::OpsRoutesRead                   => "ops:routes:read",
86	            Permission::OpsRoutesWrite                  => "ops:routes:write",
87	            Permission::OpsRoutesDelete                 => "ops:routes:delete",
88	            Permission::OpsStopsRead                    => "ops:stops:read",
89	            Permission::OpsStopsWrite                   => "ops:stops:write",
90	            Permission::OpsStopsDelete                  => "ops:stops:delete",
91	            Permission::OpsTripsRead                    => "ops:trips:read",
92	            Permission::OpsTripsWrite                   => "ops:trips:write",
93	            Permission::OpsTripsDelete                  => "ops:trips:delete",
94	            Permission::OpsConfigRead                   => "ops:config:read",
95	            Permission::OpsConfigWrite                  => "ops:config:write",
96	            Permission::OpsConfigPublish                => "ops:config:publish",
97	            Permission::NotificationsInboxRead          => "notifications:inbox:read",
98	            Permission::NotificationsReadAll            => "notifications:all:read",
99	            Permission::NotificationsSubscriptionsManage=> "notifications:subscriptions:manage",
100	            Permission::NotificationsDndManage          => "notifications:dnd:manage",
101	            Permission::SysAnnouncementWrite            => "sys:announcements:write",
102	            Permission::PaymentsTransactionsRead        => "payments:transactions:read",
103	            Permission::PaymentsTransactionsWrite       => "payments:transactions:write",
104	            Permission::PaymentsRefundsRead             => "payments:refunds:read",
105	            Permission::PaymentsRefundsWrite            => "payments:refunds:write",
106	            Permission::PaymentsRefundsApprove          => "payments:refunds:approve",
107	            Permission::PaymentsReconciliationRead      => "payments:reconciliation:read",
108	            Permission::PaymentsReconciliationRun       => "payments:reconciliation:run",
109	            Permission::PaymentsStatementsRead          => "payments:statements:read",
110	            Permission::PaymentsStatementsImport        => "payments:statements:import",
111	            Permission::ReportingRead                   => "reporting:reports:read",
112	            Permission::ReportingExport                 => "reporting:reports:export",
113	            Permission::ReportingMetricsManage          => "reporting:metrics:manage",
114	            Permission::AlertsRead                      => "alerts:alerts:read",
115	            Permission::AlertsManage                    => "alerts:alerts:manage",
116	            Permission::AuditRead                       => "audit:log:read",
117	            Permission::UsersRead                       => "users:users:read",
118	            Permission::UsersWrite                      => "users:users:write",
119	            Permission::UsersDelete                     => "users:users:delete",
120	            Permission::RolesRead                       => "users:roles:read",
121	            Permission::RolesWrite                      => "users:roles:write",
122	        }
123	    }
124	}
125	
126	impl fmt::Display for Permission {
127	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
128	        f.write_str(self.as_str())
129	    }
130	}

132	// ============================================================
133	// Role → Permission mapping  (static, code-defined)
134	// ============================================================
135	
136	type PermSet = HashSet<Permission>;
137	
138	static PERMISSIONS_MAP: OnceLock<HashMap<&'static str, PermSet>> = OnceLock::new();
139	
140	/// Returns the static role-permission map, initialised once on first call.
141	pub fn role_permissions() -> &'static HashMap<&'static str, PermSet> {
142	    PERMISSIONS_MAP.get_or_init(build_map)
143	}
144	
145	/// Returns `true` if `role` holds `permission` per the static policy.
146	/// Unknown role names always return `false` (fail-closed).
147	pub fn has_permission(role: &str, permission: Permission) -> bool {
148	    role_permissions()
149	        .get(role)
150	        .map_or(false, |set| set.contains(&permission))
151	}
152	
153	// ============================================================
154	// Policy definition
155	// ============================================================
156	//
157	// Principle of least privilege:
158	//  - Every permission is explicitly listed (no wildcard / "all" grants).
159	//  - Permissions are additive; roles cannot negate another role's grants.
160	//  - RolesWrite is withheld from all predefined roles — it must be granted
161	//    only via a separate super-admin provisioning path (out of scope here).
162	//
163	// Role summary:
164	//   Operations Admin  — full ops domain, limited payment read, audit & user management
165	//   Dispatcher        — ops read/write (no delete/publish), own notifications
166	//   Finance Analyst   — full payments domain, ops read for reference
167	//   Staff User        — read-only ops, own inbox, basic reporting
168	
169	fn build_map() -> HashMap<&'static str, PermSet> {
170	    use Permission::*;
171	
172	    let mut m: HashMap<&'static str, PermSet> = HashMap::new();
173	
174	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
175	    // Operations Admin  (27 permissions)
176	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
177	    m.insert(ROLE_OPERATIONS_ADMIN, HashSet::from([
178	        // Full ops control
179	        OpsRoutesRead, OpsRoutesWrite, OpsRoutesDelete,
180	        OpsStopsRead,  OpsStopsWrite,  OpsStopsDelete,
181	        OpsTripsRead,  OpsTripsWrite,  OpsTripsDelete,
182	        OpsConfigRead, OpsConfigWrite, OpsConfigPublish,
183	        // Full notification management + announcement broadcast
184	        NotificationsInboxRead, NotificationsReadAll,
185	        NotificationsSubscriptionsManage, NotificationsDndManage,
186	        SysAnnouncementWrite,
187	        // Payment visibility + refund approval (no financial write authority)
188	        PaymentsTransactionsRead,
189	        PaymentsRefundsRead, PaymentsRefundsApprove,
190	        PaymentsReconciliationRead,
191	        // Reporting (including metric definition management)
192	        ReportingRead, ReportingExport, ReportingMetricsManage,
193	        // Anomaly alerts — full read + manage (acknowledge / close)
194	        AlertsRead, AlertsManage,
195	        // Audit trail visibility
196	        AuditRead,
197	        // User management (not RolesWrite — role schema changes require deployment)
198	        UsersRead, UsersWrite, UsersDelete, RolesRead,
199	    ]));
200	
201	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
202	    // Dispatcher  (11 permissions)
203	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
204	    m.insert(ROLE_DISPATCHER, HashSet::from([
205	        // Ops read/write — no delete, no config publish
206	        OpsRoutesRead, OpsRoutesWrite,
207	        OpsStopsRead,  OpsStopsWrite,
208	        OpsTripsRead,  OpsTripsWrite,
209	        OpsConfigRead,
210	        // Own notifications
211	        NotificationsInboxRead,
212	        NotificationsSubscriptionsManage,
213	        NotificationsDndManage,
214	        // Operational reports (read-only)
215	        ReportingRead,
216	        // Alert visibility (read-only — ops dispatchers can see alerts but not close them)
217	        AlertsRead,
218	    ]));
219	
220	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
221	    // Finance Analyst  (16 permissions)
222	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
223	    m.insert(ROLE_FINANCE_ANALYST, HashSet::from([
224	        // Ops read — reference data needed for trip-to-payment correlation
225	        OpsRoutesRead, OpsTripsRead,
226	        // Own notifications
227	        NotificationsInboxRead,
228	        NotificationsSubscriptionsManage,
229	        NotificationsDndManage,
230	        // Full payments domain
231	        PaymentsTransactionsRead, PaymentsTransactionsWrite,
232	        PaymentsRefundsRead,      PaymentsRefundsWrite, PaymentsRefundsApprove,
233	        PaymentsReconciliationRead, PaymentsReconciliationRun,
234	        PaymentsStatementsRead,   PaymentsStatementsImport,
235	        // Reporting with export (for external reconciliation review)
236	        ReportingRead, ReportingExport, ReportingMetricsManage,
237	        // Anomaly alerts — full read + manage
238	        AlertsRead, AlertsManage,
239	    ]));
240	
241	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
242	    // Staff User  (5 permissions)
243	    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
244	    m.insert(ROLE_STAFF_USER, HashSet::from([
245	        // Read-only operational access
246	        OpsRoutesRead, OpsTripsRead,
247	        // Own inbox + DND only (no subscription management)
248	        NotificationsInboxRead, NotificationsDndManage,
249	        // Basic reporting
250	        ReportingRead,
251	    ]));
252	
253	    m
254	}
255	
256	// ============================================================
257	// Tests
258	// ============================================================
259	#[cfg(test)]
260	mod tests {
261	    use super::*;
262	
263	    #[test]
264	    fn ops_admin_has_full_ops() {
265	        for perm in [
266	            Permission::OpsRoutesRead,  Permission::OpsRoutesWrite,  Permission::OpsRoutesDelete,
267	            Permission::OpsStopsRead,   Permission::OpsStopsWrite,   Permission::OpsStopsDelete,
268	            Permission::OpsTripsRead,   Permission::OpsTripsWrite,   Permission::OpsTripsDelete,
269	            Permission::OpsConfigRead,  Permission::OpsConfigWrite,  Permission::OpsConfigPublish,
270	        ] {
271	            assert!(has_permission(ROLE_OPERATIONS_ADMIN, perm), "ops_admin missing {:?}", perm);
272	        }
273	    }
274	
275	    #[test]
276	    fn dispatcher_cannot_delete_or_publish() {
277	        assert!(!has_permission(ROLE_DISPATCHER, Permission::OpsRoutesDelete));
278	        assert!(!has_permission(ROLE_DISPATCHER, Permission::OpsTripsDelete));
279	        assert!(!has_permission(ROLE_DISPATCHER, Permission::OpsConfigPublish));
280	        assert!(!has_permission(ROLE_DISPATCHER, Permission::OpsConfigWrite));
281	    }
282	
283	    #[test]
284	    fn staff_user_is_read_only() {
285	        let write_perms = [
286	            Permission::OpsRoutesWrite, Permission::OpsTripsWrite,
287	            Permission::PaymentsTransactionsWrite, Permission::UsersWrite,
288	        ];
289	        for p in write_perms {
290	            assert!(!has_permission(ROLE_STAFF_USER, p), "staff_user should not have {:?}", p);
291	        }
292	    }
293	
294	    #[test]
295	    fn finance_analyst_cannot_access_ops_write() {
296	        assert!(!has_permission(ROLE_FINANCE_ANALYST, Permission::OpsRoutesWrite));
297	        assert!(!has_permission(ROLE_FINANCE_ANALYST, Permission::OpsTripsWrite));
298	        assert!(!has_permission(ROLE_FINANCE_ANALYST, Permission::AuditRead));
299	    }
300	
301	    #[test]
302	    fn no_role_has_roles_write() {
303	        for role in [ROLE_OPERATIONS_ADMIN, ROLE_DISPATCHER, ROLE_FINANCE_ANALYST, ROLE_STAFF_USER] {
304	            assert!(!has_permission(role, Permission::RolesWrite), "{} should not have RolesWrite", role);
305	        }
306	    }
307	
308	    #[test]
309	    fn unknown_role_denied() {
310	        assert!(!has_permission("unknown_role", Permission::ReportingRead));
311	    }
312	}

1	/// Config version management: draft/publish/unpublish/schedule, diff, and
2	/// gradual rollout by depot.
3	///
4	/// Versioning strategy:
5	///   Each `config_template` has an ordered list of versions.
6	///   version_number is monotonically increasing per template.
7	///   Only one version may be `published` at a time (enforced by partial unique index).
8	///   Status transitions:
9	///     draft ──publish──▶ published ──unpublish──▶ draft
10	///     draft ──schedule──▶ scheduled ──(time/job)──▶ published
11	///     published ──rollout──▶ gradual activation per depot stage
12	///     Any ──archive──▶ archived (via admin endpoint, not exposed here)
13	///
14	/// Gradual rollout:
15	///   1. POST /rollout  → creates a RolloutPlan with N stages (10%, 50%, 100%)
16	///   2. POST /rollout/{plan_id}/stages/{stage_id}/activate
17	///      → marks stage as 'active', upserts depot_config_assignments for that stage's depots
18	use actix_web::{web, HttpResponse};
19	use uuid::Uuid;
20	
21	use crate::{
22	    auth::middleware::AuthSession,
23	    error::AppError,
24	    ops::{
25	        diff::diff_versions,
26	        models::{
27	            ConfigVersionResponse, ConfigVersionRow, CreateConfigVersionRequest,
28	            CreateRolloutRequest, DiffQuery, ListResponse, OkResponse, RolloutPlanResponse,
29	            RolloutStageResponse, RolloutStageRow, ScheduleConfigRequest,
30	            UpdateConfigVersionRequest,
31	        },
32	    },
33	    rbac::permissions::Permission,
34	    AppState,
35	};
36	
37	// ============================================================
38	// Config version CRUD
39	// ============================================================
40	
41	/// GET /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions
42	pub async fn list_versions(
43	    state:       web::Data<AppState>,
44	    session:     AuthSession,
45	    path:        web::Path<Uuid>,
46	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
47	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigRead)?;
48	
49	    let template_id = path.into_inner();
50	
51	    let rows = sqlx::query_as::<_, ConfigVersionRow>(
52	        r#"
53	        SELECT cv.id, cv.template_id, ct.key AS template_key,
54	               cv.version_number, cv.status, cv.payload,
55	               cv.effective_from, cv.effective_to,
56	               cv.published_at, cv.scheduled_at,
57	               cv.created_at, cv.updated_at
58	        FROM   ops.config_versions cv
59	        JOIN   ops.config_templates ct ON ct.id = cv.template_id
60	        WHERE  cv.template_id = $1
61	        ORDER  BY cv.version_number DESC
62	        "#,
63	    )
64	    .bind(template_id)
65	    .fetch_all(&state.db)
66	    .await?;
67	
68	    let total = rows.len() as i64;
69	    let data: Vec<ConfigVersionResponse> = rows.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect();
70	
71	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(ListResponse {
72	        data,
73	        total,
74	        page:     1,
75	        per_page: total,
76	    }))
77	}
78	
79	/// POST /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions
80	/// Creates a new draft version. If `based_on_version` is set, copies its payload as a starting point.
81	pub async fn create_version(
82	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
83	    session: AuthSession,
84	    path:    web::Path<Uuid>,
85	    body:    web::Json<CreateConfigVersionRequest>,
86	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
87	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigWrite)?;
88	
89	    let template_id = path.into_inner();
90	
91	    // Verify template exists
92	    let _template_key: Option<String> = sqlx::query_scalar(
93	        "SELECT key FROM ops.config_templates WHERE id = $1",
94	    )
95	    .bind(template_id)
96	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
97	    .await?;
98	
99	    if _template_key.is_none() {
100	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!("Template {} not found", template_id)));
101	    }
102	
103	    // Determine base payload
104	    let payload = if let Some(base_id) = body.based_on_version {
105	        let base: Option<serde_json::Value> = sqlx::query_scalar(
106	            "SELECT payload FROM ops.config_versions WHERE id = $1 AND template_id = $2",
107	        )
108	        .bind(base_id)
109	        .bind(template_id)
110	        .fetch_optional(&state.db)
111	        .await?;
112	
113	        base.map(|mut base_payload| {
114	            // Merge caller's payload on top of base
115	            if let (serde_json::Value::Object(base_map), serde_json::Value::Object(override_map)) =
116	                (&mut base_payload, &body.payload)
117	            {
118	                for (k, v) in override_map {
119	                    base_map.insert(k.clone(), v.clone());
120	                }
121	            }
122	            base_payload
123	        })
124	        .unwrap_or_else(|| body.payload.clone())
125	    } else {
126	        body.payload.clone()
127	    };
128	
129	    // Next version number for this template
130	    let next_version: i32 = sqlx::query_scalar(
131	        "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version_number), 0) + 1 FROM ops.config_versions WHERE template_id = $1",
132	    )
133	    .bind(template_id)
134	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
135	    .await?;
136	
137	    let row = sqlx::query_as::<_, ConfigVersionRow>(
138	        r#"
139	        INSERT INTO ops.config_versions
140	            (template_id, version_number, status, payload, created_by)
141	        VALUES ($1, $2, 'draft', $3, $4)
142	        RETURNING id, template_id,
143	                  (SELECT key FROM ops.config_templates WHERE id = $1) AS template_key,
144	                  version_number, status, payload,
145	                  effective_from, effective_to,
146	                  published_at, scheduled_at,
147	                  created_at, updated_at
148	        "#,
149	    )
150	    .bind(template_id)
151	    .bind(next_version)
152	    .bind(payload)
153	    .bind(session.user_id)
154	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
155	    .await?;
156	
157	    Ok(HttpResponse::Created().json(ConfigVersionResponse::from(row)))
158	}

160	/// GET /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions/{version_id}
161	pub async fn get_version(
162	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
163	    session: AuthSession,
164	    path:    web::Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
165	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
166	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigRead)?;
167	
168	    let (template_id, version_id) = path.into_inner();
169	
170	    let row = fetch_version_row(&state, template_id, version_id).await?;
171	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(ConfigVersionResponse::from(row)))
172	}
173	
174	/// PUT /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions/{version_id}
175	/// Only draft versions can be updated.
176	pub async fn update_version(
177	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
178	    session: AuthSession,
179	    path:    web::Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
180	    body:    web::Json<UpdateConfigVersionRequest>,
181	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
182	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigWrite)?;
183	
184	    let (template_id, version_id) = path.into_inner();
185	
186	    let row = sqlx::query_as::<_, ConfigVersionRow>(
187	        r#"
188	        UPDATE ops.config_versions
189	        SET    payload    = $3,
190	               updated_at = now()
191	        WHERE  id          = $2
192	          AND  template_id = $1
193	          AND  status       = 'draft'
194	        RETURNING id, template_id,
195	                  (SELECT key FROM ops.config_templates WHERE id = $1) AS template_key,
196	                  version_number, status, payload,
197	                  effective_from, effective_to,
198	                  published_at, scheduled_at,
199	                  created_at, updated_at
200	        "#,
201	    )
202	    .bind(template_id)
203	    .bind(version_id)
204	    .bind(&body.payload)
205	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
206	    .await?
207	    .ok_or_else(|| {
208	        AppError::BadRequest("Version not found or is not in draft status".to_string())
209	    })?;
210	
211	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(ConfigVersionResponse::from(row)))
212	}
213	
214	// ============================================================
215	// Publish / Unpublish / Schedule
216	// ============================================================
217	
218	/// POST /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions/{version_id}/publish
219	/// Transitions draft → published. Atomically moves any currently-published
220	/// version for this template to 'archived'.
221	pub async fn publish_version(
222	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
223	    session: AuthSession,
224	    path:    web::Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
225	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
226	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigPublish)?;
227	
228	    let (template_id, version_id) = path.into_inner();
229

429	    let (old, new) = if rows[0].version_number <= rows[1].version_number {
