23	/// POST /reconciliation/statements
24	///
25	/// Upload a daily bank/provider statement CSV for a given date.
26	///
27	/// Body (JSON):
28	/// ```json
29	/// {
30	///   "filename":            "alipay_2025-01-15.csv",
31	///   "source":              "alipay",
32	///   "content_base64":      "<base64-encoded CSV>",
33	///   "expected_fingerprint": "<sha256-hex>"   // optional
34	/// }
35	/// ```
36	///
37	/// Steps:
38	///   1. Decode base64 content.
39	///   2. Compute SHA-256 fingerprint.
40	///   3. If `expected_fingerprint` provided, verify it matches (reject on mismatch).
41	///   4. Detect duplicate file (same hash previously imported).
42	///   5. Validate CSV format strictly.
43	///   6. Store in `statement_imports` with validation metadata.
44	///
45	/// Returns 400 if the fingerprint doesn't match or the file was already imported.
46	/// Returns the import record regardless of format errors — callers can inspect
47	/// `errors` and decide whether to trigger reconciliation.
48	#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
49	pub struct UploadStatementRequest {
50	    pub filename:             String,
51	    pub source:               String,
52	    pub content_base64:       String,
53	    pub expected_fingerprint: Option<String>,
54	}
55	
56	pub async fn upload_statement(
57	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
58	    session: AuthSession,
59	    body:    web::Json<UploadStatementRequest>,
60	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
61	    session.require(Permission::PaymentsStatementsImport)?;
62	
63	    // ---- Decode ----
64	    let content = B64.decode(&body.content_base64).map_err(|e| {
65	        AppError::BadRequest(format!("content_base64 is not valid base64: {}", e))
66	    })?;
67	
68	    // ---- Fingerprint ----
69	    let actual_fp = importer::fingerprint(&content);
70	
71	    if let Some(ref expected) = body.expected_fingerprint {
72	        if !importer::verify_fingerprint(&content, expected) {
73	            return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!(
74	                "Fingerprint mismatch — expected {}, got {}",
75	                expected, actual_fp
76	            )));
77	        }
78	    }
79	
80	    // ---- Duplicate file check ----
81	    let existing_id: Option<Uuid> = sqlx::query_scalar!(
82	        "SELECT id FROM payments.statement_imports WHERE file_hash = $1",
83	        actual_fp,
84	    )
85	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
86	    .await?;
87	
88	    if let Some(eid) = existing_id {
89	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!(
90	            "File already imported — existing import_id: {}", eid
91	        )));
92	    }
93	
94	    // ---- Format validation ----
95	    let parse = importer::validate_and_parse(&content);
96	
97	    let format_errors_json = serde_json::to_value(&parse.errors).unwrap_or(serde_json::json!([]));
98	
99	    // ---- Persist import record ----
100	    let import_date = Utc::now().date_naive();
101	    let import_id: Uuid = sqlx::query_scalar!(
102	        r#"
103	        INSERT INTO payments.statement_imports
104	            (filename, file_hash, source, import_date, imported_by,
105	             raw_content_encrypted, format_errors, fingerprint_expected)
106	        VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
107	        RETURNING id
108	        "#,
109	        body.filename,
110	        actual_fp,
111	        body.source,
112	        import_date,
113	        session.user_id,
114	        content.as_slice(),
115	        format_errors_json,
116	        body.expected_fingerprint.as_deref(),
117	    )
118	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
119	    .await?;
120	
121	    // ---- Persist parsed lines (only when valid) ----
122	    if parse.is_valid {
123	        for (line_no, rec) in parse.records.iter().enumerate() {
124	            sqlx::query!(
125	                r#"
126	                INSERT INTO payments.statement_import_lines
127	                    (import_id, line_number, transaction_ref, amount,
128	                     transaction_date, description, match_status)
129	                VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, 'unmatched')
130	                "#,
131	                import_id,
132	                (line_no + 1) as i32,
133	                rec.reference.as_str(),
134	                rec.amount,
135	                rec.date,
136	                rec.description.as_deref(),
137	            )
138	            .execute(&state.db)
139	            .await?;
140	        }
141	
142	        // Mark duplicates
143	        tag_duplicate_lines(&state.db, import_id, &parse.records).await?;
144	    }
145	
146	    // Update status
147	    let status = if parse.is_valid { "completed" } else { "failed" };
148	    sqlx::query!(
149	        r#"UPDATE payments.statement_imports
150	           SET status = $2, total_records = $3, processed_records = $3, updated_at = now()

168	/// Tag duplicate lines in `statement_import_lines` after initial insert.
169	async fn tag_duplicate_lines(
170	    pool:      &sqlx::PgPool,
171	    import_id: Uuid,
172	    records:   &[super::models::StatementRecord],
173	) -> Result<(), AppError> {
174	    use super::discrepancy::{canonical_index, find_duplicates};
175	
176	    let dup_map = find_duplicates(records);
177	    if dup_map.is_empty() { return Ok(()); }
178	
179	    // For each duplicate group: look up line IDs by line_number, then set
180	    // duplicate_of_line_id on non-canonical rows.
181	    for (_ref, indices) in &dup_map {
182	        let canonical_line_no = (canonical_index(indices) + 1) as i32;
183	
184	        // Get the canonical line's ID
185	        let canonical_id: Option<Uuid> = sqlx::query_scalar!(
186	            "SELECT id FROM payments.statement_import_lines WHERE import_id = $1 AND line_number = $2",
187	            import_id,
188	            canonical_line_no,
189	        )
190	        .fetch_optional(pool)
191	        .await
192	        .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
193	
194	        let Some(cid) = canonical_id else { continue };
195	
196	        // Tag all non-canonical lines in this group
197	        for &idx in indices {
198	            let line_no = (idx + 1) as i32;
199	            if line_no == canonical_line_no { continue; }
200	
201	            sqlx::query!(
202	                r#"UPDATE payments.statement_import_lines
203	                   SET duplicate_of_line_id = $3
204	                   WHERE import_id = $1 AND line_number = $2"#,
205	                import_id,
206	                line_no,
207	                cid,
208	            )
209	            .execute(pool)
210	            .await
211	            .map_err(AppError::Database)?;
212	        }
213	    }
214	
215	    Ok(())
216	}

232	    session.require(Permission::PaymentsReconciliationRun)?;

234	    // ---- Verify the import exists and is in a usable state ----
235	    let import = sqlx::query!(
236	        "SELECT status, file_hash, raw_content_encrypted FROM payments.statement_imports WHERE id = $1",
237	        body.statement_import_id,

242

246	        ));
247	    }
248	
249	    // ---- Optional fingerprint re-verification ----
250	    if let Some(ref expected) = body.expected_fingerprint {
251	        if &import.file_hash != expected {
252	            return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!(
253	                "Fingerprint mismatch — file hash is {}, expected {}",
254	                import.file_hash, expected
255	            )));
256	        }
257	    }
258	
259	    // ---- Re-parse the stored content ----

261	        .ok_or_else(|| AppError::BadRequest("Import has no stored content".to_string()))?;
262	
263	    let parse = importer::validate_and_parse(&raw);

279	    )

297	            }),

299	    )
300	    .await
301	    .unwrap_or_else(|e| tracing::warn!(error = %e, "audit log failed"));
302

395	/// Upload a payment result file (base64-encoded in JSON body).
396	/// SHA-256 of file content prevents duplicate ingestion.
397	pub async fn upload_import(
398	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
399	    session: AuthSession,
400	    body:    web::Json<UploadImportRequest>,
401	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
402	    session.require(Permission::PaymentsStatementsImport)?;
403	
404	    let valid_formats = ["csv", "json"];
405	    if !valid_formats.contains(&body.format.as_str()) {
406	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
407	            "format must be 'csv' or 'json'".to_string(),
408	        ));
409	    }
410	
411	    // Decode base64 content
412	    let content = B64.decode(&body.content_base64).map_err(|e| {
413	        AppError::BadRequest(format!("content_base64 is not valid base64: {}", e))
414	    })?;
415	
416	    let file_hash         = sha256_hex(&content);
417	    let import_date       = Utc::now().date_naive();
418	    let encrypted_content = state.crypto.encrypt_bytes(&content)?;
419	
420	    // Duplicate detection — same file hash
421	    let existing = sqlx::query_scalar!(
422	        "SELECT id FROM payments.statement_imports WHERE file_hash = $1",
423	        file_hash,
424	    )
425	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
426	    .await?;
427	
428	    if let Some(existing_id) = existing {
429	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!(
430	            "File already imported (import_id: {})", existing_id
431	        )));
432	    }
433	
434	    let row = sqlx::query_as!(
435	        StatementImportRow,
436	        r#"
437	        INSERT INTO payments.statement_imports
438	            (filename, file_hash, source, import_date, imported_by, raw_content_encrypted)
439	        VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
440	        RETURNING id, filename, file_hash, source, import_date,
441	                  status, total_records, processed_records,
442	                  error_count, imported_by, created_at, updated_at
443	        "#,
444	        body.filename,
445	        file_hash,
446	        body.source,
447	        import_date,
448	        session.user_id,
449	        encrypted_content.as_slice(),
450	    )
451	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
452	    .await?;
453	
454	    Ok(HttpResponse::Created().json(StatementImportResponse::from(row)))
455	}

510	/// Parses the stored file content and matches lines against transactions.
511	/// Idempotent: re-running on a completed import does nothing and returns the
512	/// current state.
513	pub async fn process_import(
514	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
515	    session: AuthSession,
516	    path:    web::Path<Uuid>,
517	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
518	    session.require(Permission::PaymentsStatementsImport)?;
519	    let id = *path;
520	
521	    // Load the import row
522	    let row = sqlx::query!(
523	        "SELECT status, raw_content_encrypted FROM payments.statement_imports WHERE id = $1",
524	        id,
525	    )
526	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
527	    .await?
528	    .ok_or_else(|| AppError::BadRequest("Import not found".to_string()))?;
529	
530	    if row.status == "completed" {
531	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
532	            "Import already processed".to_string(),
533	        ));
534	    }
535	
536	    let encrypted = row.raw_content_encrypted.ok_or_else(|| {
537	        AppError::BadRequest("Import has no stored content".to_string())
538	    })?;
539	    let content = state.crypto.decrypt_bytes(&encrypted)?;
540	
541	    // Detect format from existing metadata (we store filename)
542	    let import_row = sqlx::query_as!(
543	        StatementImportRow,
544	        r#"
545	        SELECT id, filename, file_hash, source, import_date,
546	               status, total_records, processed_records,
547	               error_count, imported_by, created_at, updated_at
548	        FROM payments.statement_imports WHERE id = $1
549	        "#,
550	        id,
551	    )
552	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
553	    .await?;
554	
555	    let format = if import_row.filename.ends_with(".json") { "json" } else { "csv" };
556	
557	    // Mark as 'processing'
558	    sqlx::query!(
559	        "UPDATE payments.statement_imports SET status = 'processing', updated_at = now() WHERE id = $1",
560	        id,
561	    )
562	    .execute(&state.db)

1	/// Config version management: draft/publish/unpublish/schedule, diff, and
2	/// gradual rollout by depot.
3	///
4	/// Versioning strategy:
5	///   Each `config_template` has an ordered list of versions.
6	///   version_number is monotonically increasing per template.
7	///   Only one version may be `published` at a time (enforced by partial unique index).
8	///   Status transitions:
9	///     draft ──publish──▶ published ──unpublish──▶ draft
10	///     draft ──schedule──▶ scheduled ──(time/job)──▶ published
11	///     published ──rollout──▶ gradual activation per depot stage
12	///     Any ──archive──▶ archived (via admin endpoint, not exposed here)
13	///
14	/// Gradual rollout:
15	///   1. POST /rollout  → creates a RolloutPlan with N stages (10%, 50%, 100%)
16	///   2. POST /rollout/{plan_id}/stages/{stage_id}/activate
17	///      → marks stage as 'active', upserts depot_config_assignments for that stage's depots
18	use actix_web::{web, HttpResponse};

25	        diff::diff_versions,

27	            ConfigVersionResponse, ConfigVersionRow, CreateConfigVersionRequest,
28	            CreateRolloutRequest, DiffQuery, ListResponse, OkResponse, RolloutPlanResponse,
29	            RolloutStageResponse, RolloutStageRow, ScheduleConfigRequest,
30	            UpdateConfigVersionRequest,
31	        },
32	    },

41	/// GET /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions
42	pub async fn list_versions(
43	    state:       web::Data<AppState>,
44	    session:     AuthSession,
45	    path:        web::Path<Uuid>,
46	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
47	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigRead)?;
48	
49	    let template_id = path.into_inner();
50	
51	    let rows = sqlx::query_as::<_, ConfigVersionRow>(
52	        r#"
53	        SELECT cv.id, cv.template_id, ct.key AS template_key,
54	               cv.version_number, cv.status, cv.payload,
55	               cv.effective_from, cv.effective_to,
56	               cv.published_at, cv.scheduled_at,
57	               cv.created_at, cv.updated_at
58	        FROM   ops.config_versions cv
59	        JOIN   ops.config_templates ct ON ct.id = cv.template_id
60	        WHERE  cv.template_id = $1
61	        ORDER  BY cv.version_number DESC
62	        "#,
63	    )
64	    .bind(template_id)
65	    .fetch_all(&state.db)
66	    .await?;
67	
68	    let total = rows.len() as i64;
69	    let data: Vec<ConfigVersionResponse> = rows.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect();
70	
71	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(ListResponse {
72	        data,
73	        total,
74	        page:     1,
75	        per_page: total,
76	    }))
77	}

79	/// POST /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions
80	/// Creates a new draft version. If `based_on_version` is set, copies its payload as a starting point.
81	pub async fn create_version(
82	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
83	    session: AuthSession,
84	    path:    web::Path<Uuid>,
85	    body:    web::Json<CreateConfigVersionRequest>,
86	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
87	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigWrite)?;
88	
89	    let template_id = path.into_inner();
90	
91	    // Verify template exists
92	    let _template_key: Option<String> = sqlx::query_scalar(
93	        "SELECT key FROM ops.config_templates WHERE id = $1",
94	    )
95	    .bind(template_id)
96	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
97	    .await?;
98	
99	    if _template_key.is_none() {
100	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!("Template {} not found", template_id)));
101	    }
102	
103	    // Determine base payload
104	    let payload = if let Some(base_id) = body.based_on_version {
105	        let base: Option<serde_json::Value> = sqlx::query_scalar(
106	            "SELECT payload FROM ops.config_versions WHERE id = $1 AND template_id = $2",
107	        )
108	        .bind(base_id)
109	        .bind(template_id)
110	        .fetch_optional(&state.db)
111	        .await?;
112	
113	        base.map(|mut base_payload| {
114	            // Merge caller's payload on top of base
115	            if let (serde_json::Value::Object(base_map), serde_json::Value::Object(override_map)) =
116	                (&mut base_payload, &body.payload)
117	            {
118	                for (k, v) in override_map {
119	                    base_map.insert(k.clone(), v.clone());
120	                }
121	            }
122	            base_payload
123	        })
124	        .unwrap_or_else(|| body.payload.clone())
125	    } else {
126	        body.payload.clone()
127	    };
128	
129	    // Next version number for this template
130	    let next_version: i32 = sqlx::query_scalar(
131	        "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version_number), 0) + 1 FROM ops.config_versions WHERE template_id = $1",
132	    )
133	    .bind(template_id)
134	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
135	    .await?;
136	
137	    let row = sqlx::query_as::<_, ConfigVersionRow>(
138	        r#"
139	        INSERT INTO ops.config_versions
140	            (template_id, version_number, status, payload, created_by)
141	        VALUES ($1, $2, 'draft', $3, $4)
142	        RETURNING id, template_id,
143	                  (SELECT key FROM ops.config_templates WHERE id = $1) AS template_key,
144	                  version_number, status, payload,
145	                  effective_from, effective_to,
146	                  published_at, scheduled_at,
147	                  created_at, updated_at
148	        "#,
149	    )
150	    .bind(template_id)
151	    .bind(next_version)
152	    .bind(payload)
153	    .bind(session.user_id)
154	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
155	    .await?;
156	
157	    Ok(HttpResponse::Created().json(ConfigVersionResponse::from(row)))
158	}

218	/// POST /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions/{version_id}/publish
219	/// Transitions draft → published. Atomically moves any currently-published
220	/// version for this template to 'archived'.
221	pub async fn publish_version(
222	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
223	    session: AuthSession,
224	    path:    web::Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
225	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
226	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigPublish)?;
227	
228	    let (template_id, version_id) = path.into_inner();
229	
230	    let mut tx = state.db.begin().await?;
231	
232	    // Archive current published version (if any)
233	    sqlx::query(
234	        r#"
235	        UPDATE ops.config_versions
236	        SET    status = 'archived', updated_at = now()
237	        WHERE  template_id = $1 AND status = 'published'
238	        "#,
239	    )
240	    .bind(template_id)
241	    .execute(&mut *tx)
242	    .await?;
243	
244	    // Publish the target version
245	    let affected = sqlx::query(
246	        r#"
247	        UPDATE ops.config_versions
248	        SET    status       = 'published',
249	               published_at = now(),
250	               updated_at   = now()
251	        WHERE  id           = $1
252	          AND  template_id  = $2
253	          AND  status       IN ('draft', 'scheduled')
254	        "#,
255	    )
256	    .bind(version_id)
257	    .bind(template_id)
258	    .execute(&mut *tx)
259	    .await?
260	    .rows_affected();
261	
262	    if affected == 0 {
263	        tx.rollback().await?;
264	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
265	            "Version not found or is not in draft/scheduled status".to_string(),
266	        ));
267	    }
268	
269	    tx.commit().await?;
270	
271	    crate::audit::writer::log(
272	        &state.db,
273	        &session,
274	        crate::audit::writer::AuditEntry {
275	            action:       crate::audit::writer::ACTION_CONFIG_PUBLISH,
276	            domain:       "ops",
277	            entity_type:  "config_version",
278	            entity_id:    version_id.to_string(),
279	            before_state: None,
280	            after_state:  None,
281	            metadata:     serde_json::json!({ "template_id": template_id }),
282	        },
283	    )
284	    .await
285	    .unwrap_or_else(|e| tracing::warn!(error = %e, "audit log failed"));
286	
287	    tracing::info!(
288	        template_id = %template_id,
289	        version_id  = %version_id,
290	        user_id     = %session.user_id,
291	        "Config version published"
292	    );
293	
294	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(OkResponse { message: "Version published" }))
295	}

350	/// POST /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions/{version_id}/schedule
351	/// Sets status = 'scheduled' with a future effective_from.
352	/// A background scheduler (e.g. pg_cron or app-level cron) calls `publish_version`
353	/// when `effective_from` is reached.
354	pub async fn schedule_version(
355	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
356	    session: AuthSession,
357	    path:    web::Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
358	    body:    web::Json<ScheduleConfigRequest>,
359	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
360	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigPublish)?;
361	
362	    let (template_id, version_id) = path.into_inner();
363	
364	    if body.effective_from <= chrono::Utc::now() {
365	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
366	            "effective_from must be in the future".to_string(),
367	        ));
368	    }
369	
370	    if let Some(to) = body.effective_to {
371	        if to <= body.effective_from {
372	            return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
373	                "effective_to must be after effective_from".to_string(),
374	            ));
375	        }
376	    }
377	
378	    let affected = sqlx::query(
379	        r#"
380	        UPDATE ops.config_versions
381	        SET    status         = 'scheduled',
382	               scheduled_at  = $3,
383	               effective_from = $3,
384	               effective_to   = $4,
385	               updated_at     = now()
386	        WHERE  id             = $1
387	          AND  template_id    = $2
388	          AND  status         = 'draft'
389	        "#,
390	    )
391	    .bind(version_id)
392	    .bind(template_id)
393	    .bind(body.effective_from)
394	    .bind(body.effective_to)
395	    .execute(&state.db)
396	    .await?
397	    .rows_affected();
398	
399	    if affected == 0 {
400	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
401	            "Version not found or is not in draft status".to_string(),
402	        ));
403	    }
404	
405	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(serde_json::json!({
406	        "message":      "Version scheduled for publication",
407	        "effective_from": body.effective_from,
408	        "effective_to":   body.effective_to
409	    })))
410	}

416	/// GET /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions/diff?v1={uuid}&v2={uuid}
417	///
418	/// Returns a structural diff between two version payloads.
419	/// Both versions must belong to the same template_id.
420	pub async fn diff_config_versions(
421	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
422	    session: AuthSession,
423	    path:    web::Path<Uuid>,
424	    query:   web::Query<DiffQuery>,
425	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
426	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigRead)?;
427	
428	    let template_id = path.into_inner();
429	
430	    if query.v1 == query.v2 {
431	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest("v1 and v2 must be different versions".to_string()));
432	    }
433	
434	    // Load both versions in a single query; validate they belong to this template
435	    let rows = sqlx::query_as::<_, ConfigVersionRow>(
436	        r#"
437	        SELECT cv.id, cv.template_id, ct.key AS template_key,
438	               cv.version_number, cv.status, cv.payload,
439	               cv.effective_from, cv.effective_to,
440	               cv.published_at, cv.scheduled_at,
441	               cv.created_at, cv.updated_at
442	        FROM   ops.config_versions cv
443	        JOIN   ops.config_templates ct ON ct.id = cv.template_id
444	        WHERE  cv.id IN ($1, $2) AND cv.template_id = $3
445	        ORDER  BY cv.version_number ASC
446	        "#,
447	    )
448	    .bind(query.v1)
449	    .bind(query.v2)
450	    .bind(template_id)
451	    .fetch_all(&state.db)
452	    .await?;
453	
454	    if rows.len() < 2 {
455	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
456	            "One or both versions not found for this template".to_string(),
457	        ));
458	    }
459	
460	    // Determine which is older/newer by version_number
461	    let (old, new) = if rows[0].version_number <= rows[1].version_number {
462	        (&rows[0], &rows[1])
463	    } else {
464	        (&rows[1], &rows[0])
465	    };
466	
467	    let diff = diff_versions(
468	        &old.payload,
469	        &new.payload,
470	        old.version_number.to_string(),
471	        new.version_number.to_string(),
472	    );
473	
474	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(diff))
475	}

479	// ============================================================

481	/// POST /ops/configs/{template_id}/versions/{version_id}/rollout
482	///
483	/// Creates a rollout plan with ordered stages.  The config_version must be
484	/// 'published'.  Stages should cover 100% of depots collectively.
485	pub async fn create_rollout(
486	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
487	    session: AuthSession,
488	    path:    web::Path<(Uuid, Uuid)>,
489	    body:    web::Json<CreateRolloutRequest>,
490	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
491	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigPublish)?;
492	
493	    let (template_id, version_id) = path.into_inner();
494	
495	    if body.stages.is_empty() {
496	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest("At least one stage is required".to_string()));
497	    }
498	
499	    // Validate stages are in increasing percentage order and depot lists non-empty
500	    let mut last_pct: i16 = 0;
501	    for (i, stage) in body.stages.iter().enumerate() {
502	        if stage.depot_ids.is_empty() {
503	            return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!(
504	                "Stage {} has no depot_ids",
505	                i + 1
506	            )));
507	        }
508	        if stage.target_percentage <= last_pct {
509	            return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
510	                "Stages must have strictly increasing target_percentage values".to_string(),
511	            ));
512	        }
513	        last_pct = stage.target_percentage;
514	    }
515	
516	    // Verify version is published and belongs to the template
517	    let status: Option<String> = sqlx::query_scalar(
518	        "SELECT status FROM ops.config_versions WHERE id = $1 AND template_id = $2",
519	    )
520	    .bind(version_id)
521	    .bind(template_id)
522	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
523	    .await?;
524	
525	    match status.as_deref() {
526	        Some("published") => {}
527	        Some(s) => {
528	            return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!(
529	                "Config version must be published before creating a rollout (current: {})",
530	                s
531	            )))
532	        }
533	        None => {
534	            return Err(AppError::BadRequest(
535	                "Config version not found for this template".to_string(),
536	            ))
537	        }
538	    }
539	
540	    let total_depots: i32 = body
541	        .stages
542	        .iter()
543	        .map(|s| s.depot_ids.len() as i32)
544	        .sum();
545	
546	    let mut tx = state.db.begin().await?;
547	
548	    // Create plan
549	    let plan_id: Uuid = sqlx::query_scalar(
550	        r#"
551	        INSERT INTO ops.rollout_plans
552	            (config_version_id, status, total_depots, current_stage, created_by, notes)
553	        VALUES ($1, 'pending', $2, 0, $3, $4)
554	        RETURNING id
555	        "#,
556	    )
557	    .bind(version_id)
558	    .bind(total_depots)
559	    .bind(session.user_id)
560	    .bind(body.notes.as_deref())
561	    .fetch_one(&mut *tx)
562	    .await?;
563	
564	    // Create stages
565	    let mut stage_responses = Vec::new();
566	    for (i, spec) in body.stages.iter().enumerate() {
567	        let stage_number = (i + 1) as i16;
568	        let stage_row = sqlx::query_as::<_, RolloutStageRow>(
569	            r#"
570	            INSERT INTO ops.rollout_stages
571	                (plan_id, stage_number, target_percentage, depot_ids, status, scheduled_at)
572	            VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, 'pending', $5)
573	            RETURNING id, stage_number, target_percentage, depot_ids,
574	                      status, scheduled_at, activated_at
575	            "#,
576	        )
577	        .bind(plan_id)
578	        .bind(stage_number)
579	        .bind(spec.target_percentage)
580	        .bind(&spec.depot_ids)
581	        .bind(spec.scheduled_at)
582	        .fetch_one(&mut *tx)
583	        .await?;
584	
585	        stage_responses.push(RolloutStageResponse {
586	            id:                stage_row.id,
587	            stage_number:      stage_row.stage_number,
588	            target_percentage: stage_row.target_percentage,
589	            depot_count:       stage_row.depot_ids.len(),
590	            status:            stage_row.status,
591	            scheduled_at:      stage_row.scheduled_at,
592	            activated_at:      stage_row.activated_at,
593	        });
594	    }
595	
596	    tx.commit().await?;
597	
598	    tracing::info!(
599	        plan_id    = %plan_id,
600	        version_id = %version_id,
601	        stages     = body.stages.len(),
602	        "Rollout plan created"
603	    );
604	
605	    Ok(HttpResponse::Created().json(RolloutPlanResponse {
606	        id:                plan_id,
607	        config_version_id: version_id,
608	        status:            "pending".to_string(),
609	        total_depots,
610	        current_stage:     0,
611	        stages:            stage_responses,
612	        created_at:        chrono::Utc::now(),
613	    }))
614	}

616	/// POST /ops/configs/{template_id}/rollout/{plan_id}/stages/{stage_id}/activate
617	///
618	/// Activates a rollout stage:
619	///   1. Marks the stage as 'active'
620	///   2. Upserts depot_config_assignments for every depot in this stage
621	///   3. Advances rollout_plan.current_stage
622	///   4. If all stages complete, marks plan as 'completed'
623	pub async fn activate_rollout_stage(
624	    state:   web::Data<AppState>,
625	    session: AuthSession,
626	    path:    web::Path<(Uuid, Uuid, Uuid)>,
627	) -> Result<HttpResponse, AppError> {
628	    session.require(Permission::OpsConfigPublish)?;
629	
630	    let (template_id, plan_id, stage_id) = path.into_inner();
631	
632	    // Load stage (validates plan ownership)
633	    let stage = sqlx::query_as::<_, RolloutStageRow>(
634	        r#"
635	        SELECT rs.id, rs.stage_number, rs.target_percentage,
636	               rs.depot_ids, rs.status, rs.scheduled_at, rs.activated_at
637	        FROM   ops.rollout_stages rs
638	        JOIN   ops.rollout_plans  rp ON rp.id = rs.plan_id
639	        WHERE  rs.id = $1 AND rs.plan_id = $2 AND rp.config_version_id IN (
640	            SELECT id FROM ops.config_versions WHERE template_id = $3
641	        )
642	        "#,
643	    )
644	    .bind(stage_id)
645	    .bind(plan_id)
646	    .bind(template_id)
647	    .fetch_optional(&state.db)
648	    .await?
649	    .ok_or_else(|| AppError::BadRequest("Stage not found for this plan/template".to_string()))?;
650	
651	    if stage.status != "pending" {
652	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!(
653	            "Stage is already {}",
654	            stage.status
655	        )));
656	    }
657	
658	    // Load config_version_id from the plan
659	    let (config_version_id, previous_stage): (Uuid, i32) = sqlx::query_as(
660	        "SELECT config_version_id, current_stage FROM ops.rollout_plans WHERE id = $1",
661	    )
662	    .bind(plan_id)
663	    .fetch_one(&state.db)
664	    .await?;
665	
666	    // Enforce sequential stage activation
667	    if stage.stage_number as i32 != previous_stage + 1 {
668	        return Err(AppError::BadRequest(format!(
669	            "Must activate stage {} before stage {}",
670	            previous_stage + 1,
671	            stage.stage_number
672	        )));
673	    }
674	
675	    let mut tx = state.db.begin().await?;
676	
677	    // Activate stage
678	    sqlx::query(
679	        r#"
680	        UPDATE ops.rollout_stages
681	        SET    status       = 'active',
682	               activated_at = now(),
683	               activated_by = $2,
684	               updated_at   = now()
685	        WHERE  id = $1
686	        "#,
687	    )
688	    .bind(stage_id)
689	    .bind(session.user_id)
690	    .execute(&mut *tx)
691	    .await?;
692	
693	    // Upsert depot_config_assignments for every depot in this stage
694	    for depot_id in &stage.depot_ids {
695	        sqlx::query(
696	            r#"
697	            INSERT INTO ops.depot_config_assignments
698	                (depot_id, template_id, config_version_id, rollout_stage_id, assigned_by)
699	            VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)
700	            ON CONFLICT (depot_id, template_id) DO UPDATE
701	                SET config_version_id = EXCLUDED.config_version_id,
702	                    rollout_stage_id  = EXCLUDED.rollout_stage_id,
703	                    assigned_at       = now(),
704	                    assigned_by       = EXCLUDED.assigned_by
705	            "#,
706	        )
707	        .bind(depot_id)
708	        .bind(template_id)
709	        .bind(config_version_id)
710	        .bind(stage_id)
711	        .bind(session.user_id)
712	        .execute(&mut *tx)
713	        .await?;
714	    }
715	
716	    // Advance plan counter; check if all stages are now active → mark plan completed
717	    let total_stages: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
718	        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.rollout_stages WHERE plan_id = $1",
719	    )
720	    .bind(plan_id)
721	    .fetch_one(&mut *tx)
722	    .await?;
723	
724	    let new_stage = previous_stage + 1;
725	    let plan_status = if new_stage as i64 == total_stages {
726	        // Mark all stages completed
727	        sqlx::query(
728	            "UPDATE ops.rollout_stages SET status = 'completed', updated_at = now() WHERE plan_id = $1 AND status = 'active'",
729	        )
730	        .bind(plan_id)
731	        .execute(&mut *tx)
732	        .await?;
733	        "completed"
734	    } else {
735	        "active"
736	    };
737	
738	    sqlx::query(
739	        r#"
740	        UPDATE ops.rollout_plans
741	        SET    current_stage = $2, status = $3, updated_at = now()
742	        WHERE  id = $1
743	        "#,
744	    )
745	    .bind(plan_id)
746	    .bind(new_stage)
747	    .bind(plan_status)
748	    .execute(&mut *tx)
749	    .await?;
750	
751	    tx.commit().await?;
752	
753	    tracing::info!(
754	        plan_id      = %plan_id,
755	        stage_id     = %stage_id,
756	        stage_number = %stage.stage_number,
757	        depot_count  = stage.depot_ids.len(),
758	        "Rollout stage activated"
759	    );
760	
761	    Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(serde_json::json!({
762	        "message":       "Stage activated",
763	        "stage_number":  stage.stage_number,
764	        "depots_updated": stage.depot_ids.len(),
765	        "plan_status":   plan_status
766	    })))
767	}

10	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

14	    CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'active', 'inactive', 'scheduled'));
15	
16	-- Entity version counter (increments on every mutation for optimistic locking)
17	ALTER TABLE ops.routes
18	    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS entity_version  INTEGER     NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,

30	    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS entity_version  INTEGER     NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,

117	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Migration 013: Background job scheduler
--
-- Creates scheduler.job_runs for execution history and outcome tracking.
-- Distributed mutual exclusion is handled via pg_advisory_lock (in-memory,
-- session-scoped) so no lock table is needed.
-- =============================================================================

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS scheduler;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Execution history
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE scheduler.job_runs (
    id           UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    job_name     TEXT         NOT NULL,
    -- 'running'  — lock acquired, execution in progress
    -- 'success'  — completed without error
    -- 'failed'   — run() returned Err
    -- 'skipped'  — advisory lock was held by another instance
    status       TEXT         NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running'
                              CHECK (status IN ('running', 'success', 'failed', 'skipped')),
    started_at   TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    finished_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
    duration_ms  INTEGER,                    -- set on completion
    outcome      JSONB,                      -- job-specific summary (success only)
    error_msg    TEXT                        -- error description (failed only)
);

-- per-job history, most-recent-first
CREATE INDEX idx_job_runs_name_time
    ON scheduler.job_runs (job_name, started_at DESC);

-- find stale running records on restart
CREATE INDEX idx_job_runs_running
    ON scheduler.job_runs (started_at)
    WHERE status = 'running';

COMMENT ON TABLE scheduler.job_runs IS
    'Append-only execution log written by the in-process scheduler. '
    'Rows with status=running and started_at older than 1 hour are '
    'artefacts of a crashed process and are repaired to status=failed '
    'during the next startup (Scheduler::recover_stale_runs).';

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON scheduler.job_runs TO transitops_app;
"}

---

## What was implemented

### Migration (`013_scheduler.sql`)
`scheduler.job_runs` — one row per execution attempt. Columns: `job_name`, `status` (`running` / `success` / `failed` / `skipped`), `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration_ms`, `outcome` (JSONB), `error_msg`. Two indexes: per-job history + stale-record scan.

### `src/scheduler/mod.rs` — core types

```
Job trait          name(), interval(), lock_timeout(), run()
ShutdownFlag       Arc<AtomicBool> — shared across all job tasks
Scheduler          spawn(job), recover_stale_runs(), shutdown_flag()
```

`recover_stale_runs()` is called once at startup. It finds any `running` records older than one hour (artefacts of a crashed process) and marks them `failed` — the only form of state repair needed.

### `src/scheduler/executor.rs` — execution engine

Every call to `execute()` does exactly this:

```
1. pg_try_advisory_lock(fnv1a(job.name))   → skip if held elsewhere
2. INSERT job_runs (status = 'running')
3. job.run(pool)                            → actual work
4. pg_advisory_unlock(lock_id)
5. UPDATE job_runs (status, duration_ms, outcome/error_msg)
```

Advisory locks are **session-scoped** in PostgreSQL — the database releases them automatically when the connection dies, so a crashed process never holds a lock permanently.

The FNV-1a hash in `advisory_lock_id()` maps job names to stable `i64` values that require no lock table and survive restarts.

### Six jobs

| Job | Module wraps | Interval | Key idempotency mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notification_bus` | `bus::tick_once` | 5 s | `WHERE processed_at IS NULL LIMIT 50`; DND flush is a single UPDATE |
| `payment_compensation` | `compensation::run_all_sweeps` | 15 min | `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` + status guards |
| `report_generation` | `reporting::scheduler::tick` | 60 s | `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on `scheduled_reports` |
| `kpi_anomaly_check` | `detector::run_kpi_anomaly_check` | 30 min | partial unique index on `(alert_type, source_entity_id) WHERE status='open'` |
| `scheduled_config_publish` | **new** | 60 s | `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on `config_versions`; `UPDATE … WHERE status='scheduled'` |
| `dedup_cleanup` | **new** | 1 h | Time-bounded DELETEs; re-running is a no-op |

### Execution guarantees

**At-least-once, with strong deduplication:**

- Under normal conditions (single process): exactly once per interval
- During a rolling deploy (two processes share the DB): the second process always sees the lock held and skips — effectively still once
- Process crash mid-job: PostgreSQL releases the advisory lock when the TCP session closes; next instance picks up on its next tick; idempotent job logic makes re-execution safe
- Transient DB failure during start-record write: job still runs; logged as "unrecorded run"
- Transient DB failure during finish-record write: status stays `running`; `recover_stale_runs()` on next restart repairs it to `failed`

    const OFFSET: u64 = 14_695_981_039_346_656_037;
    const PRIME:  u64 = 1_099_511_628_211;
    let mut h = OFFSET;
    for b in name.bytes() { h ^= b as u64; h = h.wrapping_mul(PRIME); }

}

    dnd_start:   Option<chrono::NaiveTime>,
    dnd_end:     Option<chrono::NaiveTime>,
    now:         chrono::NaiveTime,

    match (dnd_start, dnd_end) {

            if start <= end { now >= start && now <= end }

- **`query_as!` macro incompatibility with new encrypted columns**: `TransactionRow` gained `card_last4_encrypted` and `payer_ref_encrypted` fields in the prior session, but handler queries didn't include those columns. With `query_as!`, this causes a compile error because the macro maps by position and expects all struct fields. Fix: switched all affected transaction queries to non-macro `sqlx::query_as::<_, TransactionRow>()` which maps by column name at runtime, avoiding the need to update the sqlx offline query cache.

- **`From<TransactionRow>` can't accept crypto parameter**: The standard `From` trait takes no extra parameters, so it can't decrypt fields during conversion. Fix: replaced `From<TransactionRow> for TransactionResponse` with `TransactionResponse::from_row(row, crypto)` associated function.

5. Problem Solving:

- **Data protection completion**: Ensured the encrypt/decrypt round-trip is correct: fingerprint/hash computed from plaintext BEFORE encryption (upload path), then stored encrypted; decrypt BEFORE parsing on read path.
- **Non-macro sqlx query approach**: Using `sqlx::query_as::<_, TransactionRow>(sql)` with explicit column list including `card_last4_encrypted, payer_ref_encrypted` and `amount::double precision AS amount` aliasing avoids compile-time DB validation while being fully correct at runtime.
- **Yew architecture**: Designed independent context slices to prevent cross-domain re-renders; `SyncQueue` in IndexedDB survives page reloads; `NetworkWatcher` uses browser `online`/`offline` events.
- **Scheduler design**: Used PostgreSQL advisory locks rather than a lock table because they are session-scoped (auto-released on crash), in-memory (no table I/O overhead), and non-blocking (`pg_try_advisory_lock` vs `pg_advisory_lock`).
- **Existing tasks integration**: The four pre-existing `loop { ... sleep }` tasks were refactored to expose single-tick functions (`tick_once`, `tick` made public), which the new scheduler wraps. The old loop-based entry points (`run_event_bus`, etc.) were left in place but are no longer called from `main.rs`.

173	            if start <= end {
174	                now >= start && now <= end
175	            } else {
176	                now >= start || now <= end
177	            }
178	        }
179	        _ => true, // all-day DND — no time window set
180	    }
181	}
182	
183	/// Returns `true` if the user's DND window is currently active (UTC).
184	/// Returns `false` for unknown users (no preferences row).
185	pub(crate) async fn check_dnd(pool: &PgPool, user_id: Uuid) -> Result<bool, sqlx::Error> {
186	    #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]
187	    struct PrefRow {
188	        dnd_enabled: bool,
189	        dnd_start:   Option<NaiveTime>,
190	        dnd_end:     Option<NaiveTime>,
191	    }
192	
193	    let pref = sqlx::query_as::<_, PrefRow>(
194	        "SELECT dnd_enabled, dnd_start, dnd_end \
195	         FROM   notifications.preferences \
196	         WHERE  user_id = $1",
197	    )
198	    .bind(user_id)
199	    .fetch_optional(pool)
200	    .await?;
201	
202	    Ok(match pref {
203	        None                          => false,
204	        Some(p) if !p.dnd_enabled     => false,
205	        Some(PrefRow { dnd_start: Some(start), dnd_end: Some(end), .. }) => {
206	            let now = Utc::now().naive_utc().time();
207	            if start <= end {
208	                now >= start && now <= end   // e.g. 08:00–18:00
209	            } else {
210	                now >= start || now <= end   // crosses midnight e.g. 22:00–07:00
211	            }
212	        }
213	        _ => true, // dnd_enabled with no time window → all-day DND
214	    })
215	}
216	
217	// ── Fan-out ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
218	
219	async fn fan_out_event(
220	    pool:     &PgPool,
221	    event:    &PendingEventRow,
222	    adapters: &AdapterRegistry,
223	) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
224	    let severity   = event.effective_severity.as_str();
225	    let recipients = get_recipients(pool, event).await?;
226	
227	    for user_id in recipients {
228	        // Never notify the user who triggered the event
229	        if event.actor_id == Some(user_id) {
230	            continue;
231	        }
232	
233	        // Deduplication: skip if same (user, event_type, entity) delivered/queued within 15 min
234	        if check_duplicate(pool, user_id, &event.event_type, event.source_entity_id).await? {
235	            tracing::debug!(
236	                %user_id,
237	                event_type = %event.event_type,
238	                "Delivery suppressed: 15-min dedup window"
239	            );
240	            continue;
241	        }
242	
243	        if severity != "critical" && check_dnd(pool, user_id).await? {
244	            // Queue for inbox delivery when DND ends.
245	            // External channels are not dispatched during DND — consistent with user preference.
246	            sqlx::query(
247	                "INSERT INTO notifications.deliveries (event_id, user_id, status) \
248	                 VALUES ($1, $2, 'queued') \
249	                 ON CONFLICT (event_id, user_id) DO NOTHING",
250	            )
251	            .bind(event.id)
252	            .bind(user_id)
253	            .execute(pool)
254	            .await?;
255	        } else {
256	            // Deliver immediately to inbox
257	            sqlx::query(
258	                "INSERT INTO notifications.deliveries \
259	                     (event_id, user_id, status, delivered_at) \
260	                 VALUES ($1, $2, 'delivered', now()) \
261	                 ON CONFLICT (event_id, user_id) DO NOTHING",
262	            )
263	            .bind(event.id)
264	            .bind(user_id)
265	            .execute(pool)
266	            .await?;
267	
268	            // Dispatch to enabled external channel adapters (fire-and-forget).
269	            // Failures are logged and recorded but never abort inbox delivery.
270	            if adapters.any_available() {
271	                dispatch_channels(pool, event, user_id, adapters).await;
272	            }
273	        }
274	    }
275	
276	    Ok(())
277	}
278	
279	// ── External channel dispatch ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
280	
281	/// Dispatch a notification to all active channel adapters for which the
282	/// recipient has a preference row with `enabled = true`.
283	///
284	/// This function never returns an error — all failures are logged and written
285	/// to `channel_deliveries` so they're visible for support/debugging.
286	async fn dispatch_channels(
287	    pool:     &PgPool,
288	    event:    &PendingEventRow,
289	    user_id:  Uuid,
290	    adapters: &AdapterRegistry,
291	) {
292	    #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]
293	    struct ChanPref {
294	        channel:         String,
295	        channel_address: String,
296	    }
297	
298	    // Load all channels the user has opted into.
299	    let prefs: Vec<ChanPref> = match sqlx::query_as::<_, ChanPref>(
300	        "SELECT channel, channel_address \
301	         FROM   notifications.channel_preferences \
302	         WHERE  user_id = $1 AND enabled = TRUE",
303	    )
304	    .bind(user_id)
305	    .fetch_all(pool)
306	    .await
307	    {
308	        Ok(p)  => p,
309	        Err(e) => {
310	            tracing::warn!(%user_id, "Failed to load channel preferences: {}", e);
311	            return;
312	        }
313	    };
314	
315	    if prefs.is_empty() {
316	        return;
317	    }
318	
319	    for adapter in adapters.all() {
320	        if !adapter.is_available() {
321	            continue;
322	        }
323	
324	        let channel = adapter.channel();
325	
326	        let Some(pref) = prefs.iter().find(|p| p.channel == channel) else {
327	            continue;  // user has not opted into this channel
328	        };
329	
330	        let notif = OutboundNotification::from_event(
331	            event,
332	            user_id,
333	            pref.channel_address.clone(),
334	        );
335	
336	        let (status, error_msg) = match adapter.send(&notif).await {
337	            Ok(())  => {
338	                tracing::debug!(
339	                    channel,
340	                    %user_id,
341	                    event_type = %event.event_type,
342	                    "Channel dispatch sent"
343	                );
344	                ("sent", None)
345	            }
346	            Err(e) => {
347	                tracing::warn!(
348	                    channel,
349	                    %user_id,
350	                    event_type = %event.event_type,
351	                    "Channel dispatch failed: {}",
352	                    e
353	                );
354	                ("failed", Some(e.to_string()))
355	            }
356	        };
357	
358	        // Record outcome — ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING guards against bus retries.
359	        if let Err(e) = sqlx::query(
360	            "INSERT INTO notifications.channel_deliveries \
361	                 (event_id, user_id, channel, status, error_msg) \
362	             VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5) \
363	             ON CONFLICT (event_id, user_id, channel) DO NOTHING",
364	        )
365	        .bind(event.id)
366	        .bind(user_id)
367	        .bind(channel)
368	        .bind(status)
369	        .bind(error_msg)
370	        .execute(pool)
371	        .await
372	        {
373	            tracing::warn!("Failed to record channel delivery: {}", e);
374	        }
375	    }
376	}
377	
378	async fn get_recipients(pool: &PgPool, event: &PendingEventRow) -> Result<Vec<Uuid>, sqlx::Error> {
379	    if event.event_type == "sys.announcement" {
380	        let target_roles: Option<Vec<String>> = event
381	            .payload
382	            .get("target_roles")
383	            .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
384	            .map(|arr| {
385	                arr.iter()
386	                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))
387	                    .collect()
388	            });
389	
390	        let is_all = target_roles
391	            .as_deref()
392	            .map_or(true, |r| r.is_empty() || r == ["all"]);
393	
394	        if is_all {
395	            sqlx::query_scalar(
396	                "SELECT id FROM auth.users WHERE is_active = TRUE AND deleted_at IS NULL",
397	            )
398	            .fetch_all(pool)
399	            .await
400	        } else {
401	            let roles = target_roles.unwrap();
402	            sqlx::query_scalar(
403	                "SELECT u.id FROM auth.users u \
404	                 JOIN   auth.roles r ON r.id = u.role_id \
405	                 WHERE  u.is_active = TRUE AND u.deleted_at IS NULL \
406	                   AND  r.name = ANY($1)",
407	            )
408	            .bind(&roles)
409	            .fetch_all(pool)
410	            .await
411	        }
412	    } else {
413	        sqlx::query_scalar(
414	            "SELECT user_id FROM notifications.subscriptions WHERE event_type = $1",
415	        )
416	        .bind(&event.event_type)
417	        .fetch_all(pool)
418	        .await
419	    }
420	}
421	
422	/// Returns `true` if a non-dismissed delivery for the same
423	/// (user, event_type, source_entity_id) exists within the last 15 minutes.
424	async fn check_duplicate(
425	    pool:             &PgPool,
426	    user_id:          Uuid,
427	    event_type:       &str,
428	    source_entity_id: Option<Uuid>,
429	) -> Result<bool, sqlx::Error> {
430	    sqlx::query_scalar(
431	        r#"
432	        SELECT EXISTS (
433	            SELECT 1
434	            FROM   notifications.deliveries d
435	            JOIN   notifications.events     e ON e.id = d.event_id
436	            WHERE  d.user_id         = $1
437	              AND  e.event_type      = $2
438	              AND  (
439	                    ($3::UUID IS NULL AND e.source_entity_id IS NULL)
440	                 OR  e.source_entity_id = $3
441	              )
442	              AND  d.created_at      > now() - interval '15 minutes'
443	              AND  d.status         != 'dismissed'
444	        )
445	        "#,
446	    )
447	    .bind(user_id)
448	    .bind(event_type)
449	    .bind(source_entity_id)
450	    .fetch_one(pool)
451	    .await
452	}
453	
454	// ── DND queue flush ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
455	
456	/// Promote 'queued' deliveries to 'delivered' for every user whose DND window
457	/// is not currently active. Uses a single UPDATE to minimise round-trips.
458	///
459	/// DND-inactive conditions:
460	///   • No preferences row (no DND configured)
461	///   • dnd_enabled = FALSE
462	///   • dnd_enabled = TRUE with a time window, but that window is not currently open
463	///
464	/// All-day DND (dnd_enabled = TRUE, both times NULL) keeps deliveries queued.
465	async fn flush_dnd_queue(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<u64, sqlx::Error> {
466	    let rows = sqlx::query(
467	        r#"
468	        UPDATE notifications.deliveries
469	        SET    status       = 'delivered',
470	               delivered_at = now()
471	        WHERE  status = 'queued'
472	          AND  user_id IN (
473	              SELECT u.id
474	              FROM   auth.users u
475	              LEFT   JOIN notifications.preferences p ON p.user_id = u.id
476	              WHERE  u.is_active   = TRUE
477	                AND  u.deleted_at  IS NULL
478	                AND  (
479	                    -- No preferences row → no DND configured
480	                    p.user_id IS NULL
481	
482	                    -- DND explicitly disabled
483	                    OR p.dnd_enabled = FALSE
484	
485	                    -- DND with a time window that is NOT currently active
486	                    OR (
487	                        p.dnd_enabled = TRUE
488	                        AND p.dnd_start IS NOT NULL
489	                        AND p.dnd_end   IS NOT NULL
490	                        AND NOT (
491	                            CASE
492	                                WHEN p.dnd_start <= p.dnd_end THEN
493	                                    now()::TIME BETWEEN p.dnd_start AND p.dnd_end
494	                                ELSE
495	                                    -- crosses midnight
496	                                    now()::TIME >= p.dnd_start
497	                                    OR now()::TIME <= p.dnd_end
498	                            END
499	                        )
500	                    )
501	                )
502	          )
503	        "#,
504	    )
505	    .execute(pool)
506	    .await?
507	    .rows_affected();
508	
509	    if rows > 0 {
510	        tracing::info!(count = rows, "DND flush: promoted queued deliveries");
511	    }
512	
513	    Ok(rows)
514	}

1	/// Anomaly detection and alert generation.
     2	///
     3	/// Two detection paths:
     4	///
     5	///   1. **Reconciliation mismatches** — called directly by the reconciliation engine
     6	///      after each run.  An alert is created whenever `discrepancy_count > 0`.
     7	///      Severity: `warning` when discrepancy rate ≤ 10 items and ≤ 5 % of records;
     8	///      `critical` when above either threshold (`summary.is_high`).
     9	///
    10	///   2. **KPI anomalies** — evaluated by a background task every 30 minutes.
    11	///      For each active metric, the latest daily global snapshot value is compared
    12	///      against the rolling average of the previous 9 snapshots.  If the deviation
    13	///      exceeds `config.anomaly_threshold_pct` (default 25 %), an alert is raised.
    14	///      Severity doubles from `warning` to `critical` if deviation exceeds 2 × threshold.
    15	///
    16	/// Alert creation is idempotent: at most one **open** alert exists per
    17	/// `(alert_type, source_entity_id)` pair.  When an alert is created a notification
    18	/// event is inserted into `notifications.events` (processed_at = NULL) so the
    19	/// existing event bus fans it out within 5 seconds to subscribed users.
    20	use chrono::NaiveDate;
    21	use sqlx::PgPool;
    22	use uuid::Uuid;
    23	
    24	/// Background KPI anomaly check interval.
    25	pub const KPI_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS: u64 = 1800; // 30 minutes
    26	
    27	// ============================================================
    28	// Private metric definition row (module-level to share across fns)
    29	// ============================================================
    30	
    31	#[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]
    32	struct MetricDefRow {
    33	    id:           Uuid,
    34	    metric_key:   String,
    35	    display_name: String,
    36	    config:       serde_json::Value,
    37	}
    38	
    39	// ============================================================
    40	// Background KPI scheduler
    41	// ============================================================
    42	
    43	/// Long-running background task — call once at startup via `tokio::spawn`.
    44	pub async fn run_kpi_anomaly_scheduler(pool: PgPool) {
    45	    loop {
    46	        if let Err(e) = run_kpi_anomaly_check(&pool).await {
    47	            tracing::error!(error = %e, "KPI anomaly check failed");
    48	        }
    49	        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(KPI_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS)).await;
    50	    }
    51	}
    52	
    53	/// Single KPI anomaly detection pass.  Errors in one metric do not abort others.
    54	pub async fn run_kpi_anomaly_check(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
    55	    let defs = sqlx::query_as!(
    56	        MetricDefRow,
    57	        "SELECT id, metric_key, display_name, config
    58	         FROM   reporting.metric_definitions
    59	         WHERE  is_active = true",
    60	    )
    61	    .fetch_all(pool)
    62	    .await?;
    63	
    64	    for def in &defs {
    65	        if let Err(e) = check_metric_anomaly(pool, def).await {
    66	            tracing::warn!(
    67	                metric_key = %def.metric_key,
    68	                error = %e,
    69	                "KPI anomaly check skipped for metric"
    70	            );
    71	        }
    72	    }
    73	    Ok(())
    74	}
    75	
    76	// ============================================================
    77	// Per-metric anomaly check
    78	// ============================================================
    79	
    80	async fn check_metric_anomaly(pool: &PgPool, def: &MetricDefRow) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
    81	    #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]
    82	    struct SnapRow {
    83	        value: f64,
    84	    }
    85	
    86	    // Fetch the last 10 daily global (no route/depot filter) snapshots, newest first.
    87	    let snaps = sqlx::query_as!(
    88	        SnapRow,
    89	        r#"
    90	        SELECT value::double precision AS "value!: f64"
    91	        FROM   reporting.metric_snapshots
    92	        WHERE  metric_id   = $1
    93	          AND  granularity = 'day'
    94	          AND  route_id   IS NULL
    95	          AND  depot_id   IS NULL
    96	        ORDER BY period_start DESC
    97	        LIMIT 10
    98	        "#,
    99	        def.id,
   100	    )
   101	    .fetch_all(pool)
   102	    .await?;
   103	
   104	    // Need at least 3 points: 1 current + 2 baseline.
   105	    if snaps.len() < 3 {
   106	        return Ok(());
   107	    }
   108	
   109	    let latest_value = snaps[0].value;
   110	    let baseline: Vec<f64> = snaps[1..].iter().map(|s| s.value).collect();
   111	    let avg = baseline.iter().sum::<f64>() / baseline.len() as f64;
   112	
   113	    // Skip if baseline is effectively zero to avoid spurious division.
   114	    if avg.abs() < 1e-9 {
   115	        return Ok(());
   116	    }
   117	
   118	    let threshold_pct: f64 = def
   119	        .config
   120	        .get("anomaly_threshold_pct")
   121	        .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())
   122	        .unwrap_or(25.0);
   123	
   124	    let deviation_pct = (latest_value - avg).abs() / avg.abs() * 100.0;
   125	    if deviation_pct <= threshold_pct {
   126	        return Ok(());
   127	    }
   128	
   129	    // Double the threshold → critical; otherwise warning.
   130	    let severity = if deviation_pct > threshold_pct * 2.0 { "critical" } else { "warning" };
   131	
   132	    let title = format!("KPI anomaly: {}", def.display_name);
   133	    let description = format!(
   134	        "Current value {:.2} deviates {:.1}% from baseline avg {:.2} \
   135	         (threshold: {:.0}%)",
   136	        latest_value, deviation_pct, avg, threshold_pct,
   137	    );
   138	    let payload = serde_json::json!({
   139	        "metric_id":       def.id,
   140	        "metric_key":      def.metric_key,
   141	        "current_value":   latest_value,
   142	        "baseline_avg":    avg,
   143	        "deviation_pct":   deviation_pct,
   144	        "threshold_pct":   threshold_pct,
   145	        "severity":        severity,
   146	    });
   147	
   148	    create_alert(
   149	        pool,
   150	        "kpi_anomaly",
   151	        severity,
   152	        "reporting",
   153	        Some(def.id),
   154	        &title,
   155	        Some(&description),
   156	        payload,
   157	    )
   158	    .await
   159	}
   160	
   161	// ============================================================
   162	// Reconciliation mismatch alert
   163	// ============================================================
   164	
   165	/// Create (or skip if already open) a reconciliation mismatch alert.
   166	///
   167	/// Accepts primitive types only — the engine passes extracted fields so that
   168	/// this module does not need to import reconciliation types.
   169	pub async fn check_reconciliation_run(
   170	    pool:              &PgPool,
   171	    run_id:            Uuid,
   172	    run_date:          NaiveDate,
   173	    discrepancy_count: usize,
   174	    amount_mismatches: usize,
   175	    missing:           usize,
   176	    extra:             usize,
   177	    duplicates:        usize,
   178	    total_expected:    f64,
   179	    total_collected:   f64,
   180	    is_high:           bool,
   181	) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
   182	    if discrepancy_count == 0 {
   183	        return Ok(());
   184	    }
   185	
   186	    let severity = if is_high { "critical" } else { "warning" };
   187	
   188	    let title = format!("Reconciliation mismatch — {}", run_date);
   189	    let description = format!(
   190	        "{} discrepancies: {} amount mismatches, {} missing from statement, \
   191	         {} extra in statement, {} duplicates",
   192	        discrepancy_count, amount_mismatches, missing, extra, duplicates,
   193	    );
   194	    let payload = serde_json::json!({
   195	        "run_id":                 run_id,
   196	        "run_date":               run_date.to_string(),
   197	        "discrepancy_count":      discrepancy_count,
   198	        "amount_mismatches":      amount_mismatches,
   199	        "missing_from_statement": missing,
   200	        "extra_in_statement":     extra,
   201	        "duplicates":             duplicates,
   202	        "total_expected":         total_expected,
   203	        "total_collected":        total_collected,
   204	        "severity":               severity,
   205	    });
   206	
   207	    create_alert(
   208	        pool,
   209	        "reconciliation_mismatch",
   210	        severity,
   211	        "payments",
   212	        Some(run_id),
   213	        &title,
   214	        Some(&description),
   215	        payload,
   216	    )
   217	    .await
   218	}
   219	
   220	// ============================================================
   221	// Core: idempotent insert + notification event
   222	// ============================================================
   223	
   224	/// Insert an alert and notify subscribers via the event bus.
   225	///
   226	/// Skips silently if an open alert already exists for the same
   227	/// `(alert_type, source_entity_id)` pair.
   228	pub async fn create_alert(
   229	    pool:             &PgPool,
   230	    alert_type:       &str,
   231	    severity:         &str,
   232	    source_domain:    &str,
   233	    source_entity_id: Option<Uuid>,
   234	    title:            &str,
   235	    description:      Option<&str>,
   236	    payload:          serde_json::Value,
   237	) -> Result<(), sqlx::Error> {
   238	
   239	    // ---- Idempotency: skip if open alert already exists ----
   240	    if let Some(eid) = source_entity_id {
   241	        let exists: Option<Uuid> = sqlx::query_scalar!(
   242	            r#"
   243	            SELECT id FROM alerting.alerts
   244	            WHERE  alert_type       = $1
   245	              AND  source_entity_id = $2
   246	              AND  status           = 'open'
   247	            LIMIT 1
   248	            "#,
   249	            alert_type,
   250	            eid,
   251	        )
   252	        .fetch_optional(pool)
   253	        .await?;
   254	
   255	        if exists.is_some() {
   256	            return Ok(());
   257	        }
   258	    }
   259	
   260	    // ---- Insert alert ----
   261	    let alert_id: Uuid = sqlx::query_scalar!(
   262	        r#"
   263	        INSERT INTO alerting.alerts
   264	            (alert_type, severity, source_domain, source_entity_id,
   265	             title, description, payload)
   266	        VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7)
   267	        RETURNING id
   268	        "#,
   269	        alert_type,
   270	        severity,
   271	        source_domain,
   272	        source_entity_id,
   273	        title,
   274	        description,
   275	        payload,
   276	    )
   277	    .fetch_one(pool)
   278	    .await?;
   279	
   280	    // ---- Map to notification event type ----
   281	    let event_type = match alert_type {
   282	        "reconciliation_mismatch" => "alerts.anomaly.reconciliation_mismatch",
   283	        "kpi_anomaly"             => "alerts.anomaly.kpi_deviation",
   284	        _                         => {
   285	            tracing::warn!(alert_type, "unknown alert_type — skipping notification event");
   286	            return Ok(());
   287	        }
   288	    };
   289	
   290	    // ---- Fire notification event (bus picks it up within 5 s) ----
   291	    // Embed alert_id + severity so subscribers see them in the inbox payload.
   292	    let mut event_payload = payload;
   293	    event_payload["alert_id"] = serde_json::Value::String(alert_id.to_string());
   294	    event_payload["severity"] = serde_json::Value::String(severity.to_string());
   295	
   296	    sqlx::query!(
   297	        r#"
   298	        INSERT INTO notifications.events
   299	            (event_type, source_domain, source_entity_id, payload)
   300	        VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
   301	        "#,
   302	        event_type,
   303	        source_domain,
   304	        alert_id,
   305	        event_payload,
   306	    )
   307	    .execute(pool)
   308	    .await?;
   309	
   310	    tracing::info!(
   311	        alert_id = %alert_id,
   312	        alert_type,
   313	        severity,
   314	        "anomaly alert created"
   315	    );
   316	
   317	    Ok(())
   318	}
   319	
   320	// ============================================================
   321	// Tests
   322	// ============================================================
   323	#[cfg(test)]
   324	mod tests {
   325	    /// Verify the KPI check interval constant matches the 30-minute requirement.
   326	    #[test]
   327	    fn kpi_check_interval_is_30_minutes() {
   328	        assert_eq!(super::KPI_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS, 30 * 60);
   329	    }
   330	
   331	    #[test]
   332	    fn deviation_threshold_logic() {
   333	        // 25% threshold: deviation of 30% → warning; deviation of 51% → critical
   334	        let threshold_pct = 25.0_f64;
   335	        let dev_warning  = 30.0_f64;
   336	        let dev_critical = 51.0_f64;
   337	
   338	        let sev_w = if dev_warning  > threshold_pct * 2.0 { "critical" } else { "warning" };
   339	        let sev_c = if dev_critical > threshold_pct * 2.0 { "critical" } else { "warning" };
   340	
   341	        assert_eq!(sev_w, "warning");
   342	        assert_eq!(sev_c, "critical");
   343	    }
   344	}

     1	/// Pluggable notification channel adapters.
     2	///
     3	/// ## Interface contract
     4	///
     5	/// Each adapter implements [`NotificationAdapter`]:
     6	///
     7	/// ```text
     8	/// channel()       → canonical name: "email" | "sms" | "wecom"
     9	/// is_available()  → true only when the on-prem connector is configured
    10	/// send()          → dispatch one outbound notification; non-fatal failure
    11	/// ```
    12	///
    13	/// ## Enable / disable mechanism
    14	///
    15	/// Adapters are **inert by default**.  An adapter becomes active only when its
    16	/// connector URL environment variable is present:
    17	///
    18	/// | Channel | Env var            | On-prem endpoint      |
    19	/// |---------|--------------------|-----------------------|
    20	/// | email   | `EMAIL_RELAY_URL`  | Internal SMTP relay   |
    21	/// | sms     | `SMS_GATEWAY_URL`  | On-prem SMS appliance |
    22	/// | wecom   | `WECOM_WEBHOOK_URL`| WeCom Bot proxy       |
    23	///
    24	/// If the env var is absent the adapter's `is_available()` returns `false` and
    25	/// the bus skips it entirely — no network calls, no errors.  The service
    26	/// therefore works offline by default.
    27	///
    28	/// ## Registry
    29	///
    30	/// [`AdapterRegistry`] is `Clone` (cheap — wraps an `Arc`) and is passed to
    31	/// the event-bus background task at startup.  HTTP handlers do not hold the
    32	/// registry; they only manage per-user channel preferences in the DB.
    33	///
    34	/// ## Adding a new channel
    35	///
    36	/// 1. Create `src/notifications/adapters/new_channel.rs` implementing `NotificationAdapter`.
    37	/// 2. Expose it here with `pub mod new_channel`.
    38	/// 3. Instantiate it in `main.rs` and push it onto the registry builder.
    39	/// 4. Add the new channel name to the CHECK constraint in migration 012 and
    40	///    to `models::VALID_CHANNELS`.
    41	pub mod email;
    42	pub mod sms;
    43	pub mod wecom;
    44	
    45	use std::sync::Arc;
    46	
    47	use uuid::Uuid;
    48	
    49	// ============================================================
    50	// Outbound notification payload
    51	// ============================================================
    52	
    53	/// All information an adapter needs to dispatch one notification.
    54	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    55	pub struct OutboundNotification {
    56	    /// e.g. `"ops.trip.conflict_detected"`
    57	    pub event_type:      String,
    58	    /// `"info"` | `"warning"` | `"critical"`
    59	    pub severity:        String,
    60	    /// Short human-readable title derived from the event payload or event type.
    61	    pub title:           String,
    62	    /// Longer description for the message body.
    63	    pub body:            String,
    64	    /// Raw event payload for adapters that want structured data.
    65	    pub payload:         serde_json::Value,
    66	    /// Internal user ID — used for audit / correlation, not sent to channel.
    67	    pub recipient_id:    Uuid,
    68	    /// Channel-specific delivery address: email addr / E.164 phone / WeCom user ID.
    69	    pub channel_address: String,
    70	}
    71	
    72	impl OutboundNotification {
    73	    /// Build from a bus `PendingEventRow` plus channel address.
    74	    pub fn from_event(
    75	        event:           &crate::notifications::models::PendingEventRow,
    76	        recipient_id:    Uuid,
    77	        channel_address: String,
    78	    ) -> Self {
    79	        let (title, body) = derive_title_body(event);
    80	        Self {
    81	            event_type:   event.event_type.clone(),
    82	            severity:     event.effective_severity.clone(),
    83	            title,
    84	            body,
    85	            payload:      event.payload.clone(),
    86	            recipient_id,
    87	            channel_address,
    88	        }
    89	    }
    90	}
    91	
    92	/// Extract a human-readable title and body from an event's payload.
    93	///
    94	/// Respects well-known payload keys first (`"title"`, `"message"`,
    95	/// `"description"`), then falls back to the event_type string.
    96	fn derive_title_body(event: &crate::notifications::models::PendingEventRow) -> (String, String) {
    97	    let title = event.payload
    98	        .get("title")
    99	        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   100	        .unwrap_or(&event.event_type)
   101	        .to_string();
   102	
   103	    let body = event.payload
   104	        .get("message")
   105	        .or_else(|| event.payload.get("description"))
   106	        .or_else(|| event.payload.get("body"))
   107	        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   108	        .map(String::from)
   109	        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
   110	            format!(
   111	                "Event {} triggered (severity: {}).",
   112	                event.event_type, event.effective_severity
   113	            )
   114	        });
   115	
   116	    (title, body)
   117	}
   118	
   119	// ============================================================
   120	// Error type
   121	// ============================================================
   122	
   123	#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
   124	pub enum AdapterError {
   125	    #[error("adapter not configured — connector URL not set")]
   126	    NotConfigured,
   127	    #[error("delivery failed: {0}")]
   128	    DeliveryFailed(String),
   129	}
   130	
   131	// ============================================================
   132	// Trait
   133	// ============================================================
   134	
   135	/// Implemented by each channel adapter.
   136	///
   137	/// The `#[async_trait]` attribute rewrites the async method into a
   138	/// `Box<dyn Future>` return type required for object-safe dispatch via
   139	/// `Box<dyn NotificationAdapter>`.
   140	#[async_trait::async_trait]
   141	pub trait NotificationAdapter: Send + Sync {
   142	    /// Canonical channel name stored in `channel_preferences.channel`.
   143	    fn channel(&self) -> &'static str;
   144	
   145	    /// Returns `true` when the on-prem connector URL env var is configured.
   146	    ///
   147	    /// The bus calls this before every dispatch; no network I/O is performed
   148	    /// when `false`.
   149	    fn is_available(&self) -> bool;
   150	
   151	    /// Dispatch a single notification.
   152	    ///
   153	    /// Failures are non-fatal from the bus's perspective: the bus logs the
   154	    /// error and records `status = 'failed'` in `channel_deliveries`, but does
   155	    /// NOT abort inbox delivery or mark the event unprocessed.
   156	    async fn send(&self, notif: &OutboundNotification) -> Result<(), AdapterError>;
   157	}
   158	
   159	// ============================================================
   160	// Registry
   161	// ============================================================
   162	
   163	/// Holds all registered channel adapters.
   164	///
   165	/// Cheaply cloneable — the inner `Vec` is behind an `Arc`.
   166	#[derive(Clone)]
   167	pub struct AdapterRegistry {
   168	    inner: Arc<Vec<Box<dyn NotificationAdapter>>>,
   169	}
   170	
   171	impl AdapterRegistry {
   172	    pub fn new(adapters: Vec<Box<dyn NotificationAdapter>>) -> Self {
   173	        Self { inner: Arc::new(adapters) }
   174	    }
   175	
   176	    /// Iterate over all adapters regardless of availability.
   177	    pub fn all(&self) -> &[Box<dyn NotificationAdapter>] {
   178	        &self.inner
   179	    }
   180	
   181	    /// `true` when at least one adapter's connector is configured.
   182	    pub fn any_available(&self) -> bool {
   183	        self.inner.iter().any(|a| a.is_available())
   184	    }
   185	}
